♻ ☆ Toward fault-tolerant quantum computation exploiting quantum spatial distribution and gauge symmetry
Ryo Asaka
We explore how the integrated use of quantum spatial distribution (QSD), or more specifically, a superposition of both spin and position states of particles, and gauge symmetry (GS) revealed by Poulin's stabilizer formalism enhances quantum error correction. The study employs $3+2$ particles on nested squares proposed in the companion paper (arXiv:2504.07941), where three of them encode Shor's nine-qubit code and the remaining two detect errors in this code through their spin state measurements. The first result is that the GS offers resilience against three types of noise acting on a particle: arbitrary decoherence of its spin or position state, and dephasing of both states, which completely or partly destroys its QSD. To show that, we formulate a noise model unifying the above noise sources and prove the correctability of this unified model under our error-correcting scheme. The second result is that the QSD, together with the GS, provides architectural flexibility, allowing us to stack the error-correcting systems both vertically and horizontally. Indeed, we present implementations of the error detection (stabilizer measurement), logical Hadamard and Toffoli gates, and a quantum adder with the required interactions only between nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor particles. Here, our treatment of the dynamics of particles, each having spin and position degrees of freedom, under nontrivial noise and gate operations indicates that the stabilizer formalism is a powerful tool for describing quantum many-body dynamics.

♻ ☆ Spurious zero-dispersion continua in full $(2,q)$-positivity: A linear hierarchy-depth lower bound from an exactly solvable counting operator
Maho Nakata
Variational two-particle reduced-density-matrix methods impose hierarchies of semidefinite constraints. We ask whether a fixed level of such a hierarchy can recover even an elementary many-fermion spectrum, using the dispersion test, in which a value is accepted as an eigenvalue when the minimized dispersion vanishes. We study an exactly solvable operator that counts fermions in one half of the spin orbitals. It is a sum of commuting occupation numbers, so its spectral problem is classical, a Boolean occupation-number problem with integer spectrum, and the obstruction found here is not a genuinely quantum one. We determine the complete set of accepted values at every level of the full hierarchy of particle-hole semidefinite constraints. Besides the integers, this set contains an entire interval of noninteger values unless the hierarchy level grows linearly with the particle number, and we give the exact threshold. The proof constructs explicit q-positive reduced density matrices, diagonal in the occupation basis, by continuing the occupation probabilities of a fixed-particle-number state to a noninteger particle number. The fermionic content is that classical semidefinite constraints on occupation correlations, with nonnegative occupation-pattern probabilities, imply positivity of every particle-hole block, so the noncommuting fermionic conditions remove no false value. A converse argument shows that no other false eigenvalues occur. The limitation is specific to the hierarchy: two-body inequalities that encode the integer spectrum would remove every false value but are not generated at a fixed level. By Erdahl's duality theorem, whose hypotheses we check at fixed particle number, the result applies equally to the full (2,q)-positivity conditions of the constructive solution of the N-representability problem.

♻ ☆ Imprints of information scrambling on eigenstates of a quantum chaotic system
Bikram Pain, Ratul Thakur, Sthitadhi Roy
How are the spatial and temporal patterns of information scrambling in locally interacting quantum many-body systems imprinted on the eigenstates of the system's time-evolution operator? We address this question by identifying statistical correlations among sets of minimally four eigenstates that provide a unified framework for various measures of information scrambling. These include operator mutual information and operator entanglement entropy of the time-evolution operator, as well as more conventional diagnostics such as two-point dynamical correlations and out-of-time-ordered correlators. We demonstrate this framework by deriving exact results for eigenstate correlations in a minimal model of quantum chaos -- Floquet dual-unitary circuits. These results reveal not only the butterfly effect and the information lightcone, but also finer structures of scrambling within the lightcone. Our work thus shows how the eigenstates of a chaotic system can encode the full spatiotemporal anatomy of quantum chaos, going beyond the descriptions offered by random matrix theory and the eigenstate thermalisation hypothesis.

♻ ☆ Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions
Kuan Cheng, Ruiyang Wu
We establish an equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors. The classical sampler-extractor equivalence is established by a seminal work of Zuckerman (Random Structures & Algorithms, 1997). Using this equivalence, we construct explicit strong matrix samplers with optimal randomness overhead and near-optimal sample complexity via constructing quantum-proof extractors. Specifically for matrix dimension $D$, accuracy $\varepsilon$ and failure probability $δ\leq\varepsilon$, our matrix sampler uses $$ m+O_α(\log(D/δ))\text{ random bits and } O_α\!\left(\varepsilon^{-2-α}\log^{1+α}(D/δ)\right)\text{ samples}, $$ for any constant $α>0$. Compared with the matrix sampler of Xun and Zuckerman (CCC 2025), our construction has improvements in two aspects. Under optimal random seed length, we can replace the $\operatorname{poly} D$ dependence in the number of samples by $O(\log^{1+α} D)$. Under the same scale of sample size, we can remove their $\log\log D$ factor in the length of the random seed. Our underlying strong quantum-proof extractor has output length $n-O_α(a+\log(1/η))$ and seed length at most $(1+α)\log a+(2+α)\log(1/η)+O_α(1)$ for $n$-bit sources with conditional min-entropy $n-a$ and error $η$. We also obtain strong quantum-proof extractors for every constant entropy rate, for any error as small as $2^{-Ω(n)}$, having optimal seed length $O(\log(n/η))$ and output length $Ω(n)$, improving previous constructions.
♻ ☆ Schrödinger Generator for High-Dimensional Integration and Sampling on Quantum Many-Body States
Lin-Jing Jiang, Fu Ma, Pei Li, Kai-Jia Sun, Guo-Liang Ma, Yu-Gang Ma
Integration and sampling in high dimensions are among central challenges in modern science and technology, underlying applications ranging from quantum many-body physics to Bayesian inference and artificial intelligence. Although conventional Monte Carlo methods are formally scalable, their efficiency deteriorates rapidly in the presence of strong correlations or sharp features in high-dimensional configuration space. Here we introduce a new framework, termed the Schr"odinger Generator, for integration and sampling based on the explicit optimization of coordinate transformations. The method decomposes the total Jacobian into two complementary components, including an adaptive map that minimizes estimator variance by learning the marginal structure in each dimension, and a normalizing-flow-based transformation that captures non-factorizable correlations in the target distribution. A final resampling step guarantees unbiased sampling even when the learned transformation is imperfect. We demonstrate stable and scalable performance for nuclear quantum many-body states in dimensions exceeding 600. Short-range correlations among nucleons in finite nucleus are faithfully reproduced. The framework offers a physically transparent approach to high-dimensional stochastic integration and sampling, opening new possibilities for simulations of complex quantum systems.

♻ ☆ Quantum Correlations of Neutrinos in the Kerr-Newman Space-time
Ze-Wen Li, Shu-Jun Rong
Quantum phases establish a connection between gravitation and quantum information, offering a novel avenue for exploring the properties of space-time. In this paper, we investigate the quantum correlations (QCs) of neutrinos in the Kerr--Newman space-time for both zero- and nonzero-angular-momentum propagation. The results show that, for zero-angular-momentum propagation, the oscillation periods of the survival probability and QCs progressively decrease with propagation distance in the inward direction. In the outward direction, increasing $M$ lengthens the oscillation periods of $P_{ν_e\rightarrowν_e}$, entanglement, and the monogamy of nonlocality, whereas increasing the angular momentum $a$ or charge $Q$ shortens them. For nonzero-angular-momentum propagation, the metric parameters also generate local profile modulations through additional two-path interference terms, rather than merely rescaling the oscillation period. Furthermore, we find that, despite differences in their ranges of variation, entanglement and coherence exhibit highly consistent oscillatory behavior in both propagation cases. These findings provide a comprehensive understanding of neutrino-based relativistic quantum information.

♻ ☆ Depth-reduced quantum simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression
Huan-Yu Liu, Cheng Xue, Yun-Jie Wang, Xi-Ning Zhuang, Chao Wang, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Guo-Ping Guo
Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors, namely restricted qubit counts and noise-limited circuit depths. In this work, we propose an efficient quantum algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on NISQ devices. For open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, we first derive a compact and stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel that approximates the target dissipative dynamics and enables ancilla-free implementation through trajectory sampling. To further reduce the circuit depth required for implementing the sampled trajectories, we introduce an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework. In this framework, a depth-adaptive parameterized quantum circuit is trained to approximate repeated Hamiltonian simulation operators, which are then used to replace repeated unitary segments appearing in the sampled trajectories. Importantly, the training procedure can also be performed without auxiliary qubits. Numerical simulations of the dissipative quantum $XY$ model and the interacting disordered $XXZ$ chain demonstrate the accuracy and reduced execution gate counts of the proposed algorithm. Our results provide a practical route toward ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware.

♻ ☆ Quantum Simulation of Non-Hermitian Special Functions and Dynamics via Contour-based Matrix Decomposition
Chao Wang, Huan-Yu Liu, Cheng Xue, Xi-Ning Zhuang, Menghan Dou, Zhao-Yun Chen, Guo-Ping Guo
Simulating non-Hermitian dynamics on quantum computers is often hindered by the decay of success probability and the instability of non-diagonalizable matrices. Here, we present contour-based matrix decomposition (CBMD), a rigorous and versatile quantum functional calculus framework for simulating non-Hermitian matrix functions. By generalizing the matrix Cauchy residue theorem, CBMD decomposes holomorphic non-Hermitian operators into an analytic infinite contour-residue identity, followed by finite truncation with controlled error to yield linear combinations of Hermitian components. For first-order dynamics, CBMD achieves optimal query complexity across all parameters, strictly matching the optimal performance bounds within the linear combination of Hamiltonian simulation (LCHS) paradigm. Beyond first-order systems, the framework naturally generalizes to complex operator functions, including second-order wave dynamics and non-Hermitian special functions such as Bessel and Airy evolutions. Furthermore, CBMD systematically suppresses the asymptotic growth of non-Hermitian components, yielding a significant reduction in the required number of amplitude amplifications compared to the naive scheme of combining monomials via linear combination of unitaries (LCU) after Taylor expansion. Notably, CBMD avoids explicit dependence on matrix diagonalizability, effectively mitigating the long-standing challenges associated with ill-conditioned eigenvectors and Jordan blocks. Our work establishes a systematic matrix calculus that bridges high-performance classical numerics and fault-tolerant quantum algorithms. It should be noted that CBMD inherits standard LCU overheads, and requires the target function to have a bounded growth order on the real axis.

♻ ☆ Operational impact of quantum resources in chemical dynamics
Julia Liebert, Gregory D. Scholes
Quantum coherence and other non-classical features are widely discussed in chemical dynamics, yet it remains difficult to quantify when such resources are operationally relevant for a given process and observable. While quantum resource theories provide a comprehensive framework for comparing free and resourceful settings, existing approaches typically rely on resource monotones or on performance bounds under free operations, and do not directly quantify the maximal influence a chosen resource can exert on a fixed chemical dynamics. Here, we introduce task specific, process level quantifiers that upper bound the largest change a quantum resource can induce in a target figure of merit. Central is a resource impact functional $\mathcal{C}_M(Λ)$, defined by comparing a state with its paired resource-free counterpart under the same quantum channel $Λ$, which admits an operational interpretation in binary hypothesis testing. We derive variation and time bounds that constrain how rapidly a resource can modify a target signal, providing resource-aware analogues of quantum speed limits. Moreover, we show that open system dynamics can be decomposed into free and resourceful components such that only the resourceful component contributes to $\mathcal{C}_M(Λ)$, thereby isolating the parts of a generator responsible for resource-induced changes in the observable. We illustrate the framework exemplary for energy transfer in a donor-acceptor dimer in two analytically solvable regimes. Our results provide a general toolbox for diagnosing and benchmarking quantum resource effects in molecular processes.
♻ ☆ Noise-induced suppression of MPO truncation errors in noisy random circuits and Lindbladian dynamics
Zhi-Yuan Wei, Joel Rajakumar, Jon Nelson, Jens Eisert, Daniel Malz, Michael J. Gullans, Alexey V. Gorshkov
We study how matrix product operator (MPO) truncation errors evolve when simulating two setups: (1) one-dimensional (1D) Haar-random circuits under either depolarizing noise or amplitude-damping noise, and (2) 1D Lindbladian dynamics of a non-integrable quantum Ising model under either depolarizing or amplitude-damping noise. We first show that the average purity of the system density matrix relaxes to a steady value on a timescale that scales inversely with the noise rate. We find that truncation errors generated at earlier steps are approximately exponentially contracted by the subsequent noisy evolution, both with system size $N$ and with the evolution depth $t$, while the cumulative error results from the competition between this contraction and newly injected compression errors. We complement the local-circuit numerics with a solvable global random-unitary model in which the same channel-dependent factor governs the mean-squared contraction of traceless errors and transient mean purity. Its exact finite-$N$ results capture the weak-noise contraction rates and the non-unital stationary-purity trend. Combining the resulting $L_2$ error characterization with the observed late-time $L_1/L_2$ conversion yields an empirical estimate of the $L_1$ truncation error that can be exponentially tighter in $N$ than the generic rank-based bound, particularly for non-unital noise. Together, these results provide empirical evidence that MPO simulation algorithms may efficiently sample from the output of 1D noisy random circuits [setup (1)] with an arbitrary number of circuit layers, and from the steady state of 1D Lindbladian dynamics [setup (2)].

♻ ☆ clifford_qc: A Python Toolkit for Quantum Simulation
Ginanjar Utama, Hermawan Kresno Dipojono
clifford_qc is a Python research toolkit for constructing quantum models, comparing variational and subspace eigensolvers, and estimating measurement resources. A common sparse Pauli algebra connects Hamiltonians, density operators, gates, and candidate-selection observables; dedicated interfaces handle circuits, execution, and statistical estimates. A worked gradient example illustrates shared measurements, and a molecular workflow separates reusable preparation, solving, and reference validation. Matrix-element banks support virtual subspaces, exact Ritz residuals, and folded-spectrum roots. Process-isolated benchmarks using the legacy density reference show that packed coefficients and streaming reduce observed peak memory on the larger tested inputs at increased runtime. Measurement studies separate setting counts, shot requirements, and device cost: fully commuting readout certifies a fixed first-order Ritz functional with fewer shots, while anticommuting cliques help some fixed reference energies and not others. Entangling-gate time and connectivity can offset shot savings or make a protocol inadmissible under illustrative device models. Further studies expose subspace bias, indeterminate encoding comparisons, failed approximate-restriction screens, and high residual-measurement costs under the tested uniform allocations. A provider workflow, scoped cost ledger, portable evidence export, and independent checks connect calculations to their recorded assumptions. Generated tables, provenance records, and manuscript checks connect claims to inputs. These small-system results support reproducible method development and establish neither hardware performance nor a general simulation speedup.

Multi-window Gabor analysis then represents the logical vector by a finite block of adjoint-lattice coefficients. We prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, obtain an explicit recovering projection, and derive stable logical reconstruction. We further construct normalizable GKP approximants as lattice-envelope Gabor multipliers and establish weak-$*$ convergence and asymptotically isometric encoding. Finally, we recover displacement syndromes from phase relations between translated coefficient blocks and quantify their stability under additive perturbations.

♻ ☆ Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
Long Huang
Process tomography built on stabilizer codes compares the logical channel of a repetition code with a reference channel, and the decoder that produces it is almost always fixed to the standard minimum-weight one. Under a fixed measurement basis, where the gate count is a resource rather than a bookkeeping artefact, we enumerate every recovery design for three, five and seven qubits and decide the rank of each exactly. The minimal counts are $0$, $1$ and $5$ single-qubit Pauli gates, against $6$, $50$ and $308$ for full decoding, and the count depends on how many sites are corrected, never on which. Correcting more sites is not monotonically better: at seven qubits full decoding has rank $24$ of $27$, proved in rational arithmetic. At the median of $40$ working points the three-gate design is $9.0$ times more precise than the six-gate decoder, and the ordering holds at every one.

♻ ☆ Pilot-waves and copilot-particles: A nonstochastic approach to objective wavefunction collapse
Axel van de Walle
We seek an extension to Schrodinger's equation that incorporates the macroscopic measurement-induced wavefunction collapse phenomenon. We find that a suitable hybrid between two leading approaches, the Bohm-de Broglie pilot-wave and objective collapse theories, accomplishes this goal in a way that is consistent with Born's rule. Our theory posits that the Bohmian particle is guided by the wavefunction and, conversely, the wavefunction gradually localizes towards the particle's position. As long as the particle can visit any state, as in a typical microscopic system, the localization effect does not favor any particular quantum state and, on average, the usual Schrodinger-like time evolution results. However, when the wavefunction develops spatially well-separated lobes, as would happen during a macroscopic measurement, the Bohmian particle can remain trapped in one lobe, which causes the wavefunction to eventually localizes. This proposed loss of ergodicity mechanism recasts one of the foundational postulate of quantum mechanics as a emergent feature and has important implications regarding the feasibility of large-scale quantum computing.

In CV protocols, homodyne detection plays a key role in the realization of the required gates and operations. Multimode squeezed light generated via parametric down-conversion (PDC) benefits from the broadband bandwidth, which encompasses multiple frequency modes. However, its broadband structure simultaneously requires the precise matching of the local oscillator (LO) with the squeezed light modes for their correct homodyne detection and processing. Achieving such matching is usually a challenging task, since the spectral bandwidth of the local oscillator is typically significantly narrower than the bandwidth of the squeezed-light modes. In this work, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a technique for expanding the bandwidth of the LO by passing it through the microstructured fiber. We validate the proposed concept by measuring squeezing in the modes of multimode squeezed light generated in type-0 and type-II PDC. We show that the broadened LO starts to spectrally match the modes generated via type-II PDC. The presented technique might be beneficial for implementing various CV systems and protocols.

The systems discussed include the anharmonic quartic oscillator as well as multivariable potentials and higher dimensional systems. For such transitions the Fermi surface as a quantum critical manifold determined by the Lee-Yang zeros, the order parameter $\mathcal{P}$ as the $d$-volume of the Fermi sea, and the special FST universality class were introduced in \cite{Chitov:2025}. The exactly solvable Hatsugai-Kohmoto (HK) $d$-dimensional ($d=1,2,3$) model of interacting fermions is analyzed. It is shown that the order parameter $\mathcal{P}$ and the FST universality class describe the transitions between metal and band/Mott insulators, as well as the Lifshitz and van Hove gapless-to-gapless transitions. The gapless phases are established to be the ferromagnetic Fermi liquids (metals), where the quantum critical manifold is also a locus of ferromagnetic order with spontaneous breaking of the rotational symmetry occurring at $T=0$. In addition to the conventional paradigm with a continuous order parameter, we apply the homology theory to analyze the FST transitions. They are critical points of the Morse function. To quantify FST we use the Euler characteristic, which is calculated for each phase of the HK model. We claim that the FST universality class is robust with respect to interactions and other model details, under the condition that the conduction band function is smooth and the critical points are non-degenerate.

Isospectrally patterned lattices exhibit a composite band structure with a tunable ratio of localized versus delocalized eigenstates that is controlled by the underlying phase gradient. We show that the lattice Hamiltonian can be interpreted as that of a single spin which, exposed to a rotating magnetic field, hops across the lattice with a spin flip. In the low- and high-energy part of the band, the localized states show an envelope of oscillatory character separated by quasi-nodes. Spin peaks occur at the locations of these quasi-nodes and provide a unique spin texture to the eigenstates, which becomes increasingly complex with increasing degree of excitation. The crossover from localization to delocalization and vice versa leaves its fingerprints in the Fourier spectrum of the eigenstates: the original bimodal frequency distribution widens with increasing degree of excitation, moves across the spectral window, and finally culminates in an extremely narrow frequency peak. In the course of this evolution, the spin texture undergoes a rearrangement transition involving different characteristic (ir)regular patterns which we quantify by considering the total variation of the local spin fluctuations. Our results demonstrate the variety of the spectral properties of isospectrally patterned lattices, which holds great prospect, in particular when considering higher lattice or cell dimensions.

We calculate several physical entities, for example, the moments and return amplitudes at large mass deformation. We calculate them for both spread complexity of states as well as Krylov growth of operators in the matrix model. We propose a general expression for the moments at any given order $n$. We also discuss orthogonal polynomials for spread as well as operator Krylov complexity. In the context of the Krylov operator growth we further compute the spectral function and the density of states. A careful analysis of the spectral function near the resonance reveals various IR divergences in addition to the physical collective modes. These collective modes appear to be exceptionally stable due to large mass gap. On the other hand, the UV of the theory appears to be extremely damped due to higher scattering rates. We carefully diagnose these IR divergences near resonance which reveals that these collective modes are in fact non-propagating and should be thought of as diffusion modes or relaxation modes with infinite relaxation time. We also calculate the Krylov variance and Krylov entropy for the matrix model and in particular at early time. The linear early time growth of the Krylov entropy confirms the onset of quantum chaos in the matrix model at large mass gap.

♻ ☆ Quantum statistics in an extended collider coupled to a qubit
Rishav Chaudhuri, Sai Satyam Samal
Mesoscopic colliders provide an effective platform for probing the mutual statistics of quantum particles. Recent experiments have successfully extracted the mutual statistics of fermions, and more exotic anyons using quantum point contacts (QPCs). Coupling a point-like collider, such as a quantum point contact, to a two-level impurity or qubit can induce statistical transmutation of fermions, causing them to display boson-like bunching tendencies. Here, we extend the analysis to an extended collider. We investigate the scattering of two incoming fermionic and bosonic wave packets in the presence of postselection on the impurity state, and systematically analyze the possible benchmarks used to characterize bunching and infer the underlying mutual statistics. We show that only a specific benchmark faithfully captures the mutual statistics of the colliding particles, while alternative choices can produce spurious statistical signatures. Hence, the correct benchmark for probing the quantum statistics depends on the intricate details of the mesoscopic collider.

☆ Existence of extremal solutions in the 1d conformal bootstrap
Filip Herček, Nat Levine
Extremal solutions and functionals play an important role in the conformal bootstrap. These are the solutions that saturate unitarity bounds, and the dual functionals that encode the optimal bounds. While they have fundamental theoretical implications, their existence has not been rigorously established. This is particularly subtle in the setting of the full infinite-dimensional bootstrap, i.e. the limit of zero numerical truncation. In this article, we prove that extremal solutions exist for OPE maximisation problems in 1d CFT. These are a large class of generically interacting, unitary, exact solutions of the crossing equation that maximise an OPE coefficient. We also prove that these problems have 'zero duality gap', meaning there exist functionals arbitrarily close to extremality. Our approach is to formulate the bootstrap as a convex optimisation problem in a Hilbert space and apply the Fenchel-Rockafellar theorem.

We show that, in the percolating phase, these fluxes dynamically reorganize into center-charge sectors whose dominant vortex tensions satisfy a Casimir scaling law, similar to that observed for confining string tensions. We then confront this result with the first nontrivial Yang-Mills case: the doubly charged vortex chains recently observed in SU(4) lattice simulations. To extract the parameters needed to connect the lattice ensemble with the effective description, we characterize how center-vortex chains grow and bend in SU(3) and SU(4) using polymer-inspired techniques not previously applied to center vortices. We find good quantitative agreement for the SU(4) doubly charged sector, providing further evidence for the proposed mechanism.

Its zeroth and first normal moments give two integrated boundary identities. The zeroth moment yields a traceless rank-two current obeying a fractonic double-divergence conservation law and a higher-rank Kac-Moody algebra. The first moment makes the normal-tangential field $w_i=h_{2i}$ explicit and yields an ordinarily conserved vector current with a standard $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra. Functional differentiation also produces a mixed equal-time bulk-boundary commutator between $w_1$ and $h_{11}$: it is non-vanishing at finite normal distance and vanishes in the intrinsic boundary limit. The equal-time commutators of the boundary current with the spatial components of the gauge-invariant field strength vanish, so microcausality is satisfied; when the boundary parameters are such that the two boundary sectors decouple, its retarded response vanishes at all times. Locally, the boundary constraints are solved by $w_i=\partial_iχ$ and $h_{ij}=\partial_i\partial_jξ+η_{ij}φ$. When the boundary parameters are such that the two sectors decouple, the induced action is the direct sum of a chiral boson in the $w_i$ sector and a higher-rank sector in which $φ$ is auxiliary and $ψ=\partial_1ξ$ is the propagating field. The latter has a non-chiral Luttinger description on its positive-energy branch and admits a chiral reduction. The boundary conditions determine the velocity and positivity branch of the $w_i$ mode, while the compatibility analysis in the $h_{ij}$ sector selects the positive-energy branch. On the positive-energy branch the two chiral modes co-propagate with orientation opposite to the sign of $κ$.

♻ ☆ Dimensional reduction and thermodynamics of a non-local scalar field theory
S. Duque Cesar, M. J. Neves
In this paper, we study the dimensional reduction of a non-local scalar field theory from $1+3$ to $1+2$ dimensions. The bulk theory is governed by an entire-function non-local form factor $e^{-\Box_E/Λ^2}$, where $Λ$ sets a fundamental high-energy scale. By constraining external classical sources to a bidimensional plane, we perform the exact dimensional reduction, derive the effective planar Green's function in terms of the complementary error function, and propose the corresponding effective non-local pseudo-differential planar Lagrangian. Using the static propagator, we determine the interaction energy between two point-like planar charges, proving that the non-local scale regularizes the short-distance singularity at the origin while smoothly recovering the standard Yukawa potential at long distances. Furthermore, we obtain the retarded, advanced, and Feynman Green's functions in coordinate space, demonstrating that macroscopic causality and tree-level unitarity are preserved. Finally, implementing the Matsubara formalism, we investigate the finite-temperature regime and evaluate the exact thermal free energy, pressure, entropy, and heat capacity. We show that the effective planar theory exhibits a fractional effective number of degrees of freedom ($g_{\rm eff}=1/2$ for $m \ll T \ll Λ$, crossing over to $g_{\rm eff}=1$ for $T \gg Λ$) originating from kinematic bulk leakage and that pressure, entropy, and heat capacity remain positive at all temperatures.
comment: 11 pages, 3 figures. Corrections were included in this version
♻ ☆ Perturbative Dissipation in Minimal Warm Inflation
Daniel J. H. Chung, Nidhi Sudhir, Lian-Tao Wang
We present an analysis of the perturbative modes of dissipation in the minimal warm inflation model where an axion-inflaton is coupled to a gluon thermal bath through the axion-gauge coupling. The corresponding friction coefficient, which generically is governed by IR physics, for the processes we consider is dominated by Landau damping of soft space-like gluons and the plasmon decay of hard on shell gluons. Since both of these processes are IR dominated, the friction coefficient becomes sensitive to the non-perturbative magnetic mass scale $m_{g}^{-1} \sim (αT)^{-1}$ which in turn leads to the friction coefficient's overall linear proportionality to $α$, which is much less suppressed in $α$ powers compared to the well understood term from Chern-Simons (CS) diffusion $(\propto α^5)$. On the other hand, this contribution to the friction coefficient is suppressed due to slow roll. We show that this can be viewed as a suppression of local spontaneous CPT violation for derivative couplings in general and that time correlations of nonlocal variables which do not fall off at large time separations are what allow an unsuppressed friction coefficient.
comment: 46 pages, 4 figures
♻ ☆ Cancellation of one-loop time dependence in superhorizon curvature perturbations from all scales
Keisuke Inomata
We show the conservation of the superhorizon curvature perturbations at one-loop level in spatially-flat gauge, including contributions from loop wavenumbers on all scales in the decoupling limit, $ε(\equiv -\dot H/H^2) \to 0$. In contrast to previous works, we do not assume a hierarchy $k \gg q$ between the wavenumber of the loop integral, $k$, and that of the power spectrum, $q$, and we explicitly include the regime $k \lesssim q$. Taking into account the nonlinear relation between the inflaton fluctuation and the curvature perturbation with the $δN$ formalism, we show that the apparent time dependence of the one-loop curvature power spectrum cancels once all contributions, including boundary terms, are combined consistently.
comment: 31 pages, 4 figures, v2: minor revision, published version
♻ ☆ On deforming and breaking integrability
Ysla F. Adans, Marius de Leeuw, Tristan McLoughlin
In this paper we study nearest-neighbour deformations of integrable models. After expanding in the deformation parameter, we identify four possible types of deformations. First there are deformations that simply break or preserve integrability. Then we find two different subtle cases. The first case is where the deformation is only integrable if all orders of the deformation parameter are taken into account. An example of these are the long-range deformations that appear in holographic models. The second case is when the deformation is perturbatively integrable to some order in the deformation parameter but can not be extended to an integrable model. In this paper we work this out for the XXZ spin chain and discuss the level statistics of each of these cases. We find numerical evidence that the onset of chaos occurs differently in each of these models. For the perturbatively integrable models, we find that the deformation strength at which chaos appears demonstrates a volume-scaling intermediate between strong and weak integrability breaking models.
comment: 24 pages, 7 figures
♻ ☆ Matter Spectral Functions from Quantum Gravity
Varun Kher, Brandon King, Daniel F. Litim, Manuel Reichert
We investigate Lorentzian quantum gravity coupled to a template matter sector with gauge fields, scalars and fermions. In the absence of quantised gravity, the matter sector by itself is renormalisable, but UV-incomplete. Provided quantum gravity offers an asymptotically safe UV-completion, we determine the photon and scalar two-point functions in the presence of gravitational fluctuations, and show that both possess a Källén-Lehmann spectral representation. Our results are achieved using functional renormalisation adapted for theories in Lorentzian signature. We explain why and how interactions with gravity modify both the infrared as well as the ultraviolet behaviour of matter spectral functions. We further determine the corresponding form factors on the level of the quantum effective action. Limitations and extensions of our study are discussed alongside implications for particle physics and unitarity of quantum gravity with matter.
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures
♻ ☆ Canonical quantization of all minisuperspaces with consistent symmetry reductions
Poula Tadros, Ivan Kolář, Otakar Svítek
We present the quantization of all symmetry reductions of the Einstein--Hilbert Lagrangian that correctly reproduce the reduced Einstein's field equations -- i.e., characterized by the infinitesimal group actions obeying the principle of symmetric criticality. These correspond to the spacetime symmetries of spherical/hyperbolic/planar Schwarzschild/Taub--NUT, BI/BII/BIII-metrics, near-horizon extreme Kerr geometry, swirling universe, closed/open/flat FLRW cosmologies, other FLRW-type metrics, and Bianchi type I, II, VIII, and IX spacetimes. We derive the Hamiltonian and the conformal symmetries of the superspace metrics (the conditional symmetries), promote them to operators, and solve the Wheeler--DeWitt equation with and without imposing these symmetries.
♻ ☆ Novel thermodynamic inequality for rotating AdS black holes
Hamid R. Bakhtiarizadeh
We propose a new thermodynamic inequality for stationary, asymptotically Anti-de Sitter rotating black holes, expressed in terms of their angular momentum, mass and thermodynamic volume as $ 4πJ^2/(3MV)<1 $. For the solutions considered, this inequality follows from the requirement that the thermodynamic identities admit a physical horizon with positive area. We examine Kerr(-Newman)-AdS, Kerr-Sen-AdS, pairwise-equal four-charge AdS black holes, charged rotating AdS black strings, and charged rotating AdS C-metrics, finding strong supporting evidence for the inequality across different horizon topologies. We then reformulate the inequality in terms of the underlying metric parameters and compare the resulting constraints with the corresponding regularity and horizon-existence conditions. This analysis shows that the proposed inequality has different physical content for different geometries. We further examine charged super-entropic black holes, for which the ultraspinning limit leads instead to a lower bound on the thermodynamic ratio. This result is consistent with the violation of the reverse isoperimetric inequality characteristic of super-entropic solutions. Moreover, when combined with the refined reverse isoperimetric inequality, the proposed bound ensures the physicality of the Kerr-AdS reference solution entering the refined bound and thereby yields the conventional reverse isoperimetric inequality. We also extend the proposed relation to higher dimensions and test it for singly spinning thin AdS black ring with nonspherical horizon topology, finding that the corresponding inequalities are satisfied throughout the thin-ring regime.
comment: 34 pages, no figure, LaTeX file. v2: New verification for Kerr-Sen-AdS. v3: Text refined; Conclusions added. v4: Revised and substantially expanded; The relation to the refined reverse isoperimetric inequality and the ultraspinning/super-entropic case are further analyzed; The higher-dimensional conjecture is tested for thin AdS black rings with nonspherical horizon topology
♻ ☆ Chiral spin symmetry
L. Ya. Glozman
We review the chiral spin symmetry, which is a symmetry of the color charge and of the confining electric part of QCD. Observation of this symmetry in the vacuum upon truncation of the near-zero modes of the Dirac operator implies that the hadron mass in the light quark sector is not due to the quark condensate of the vacuum and that confinement and chiral symmetry breaking are not directly related. Observation of this symmetry above the chiral symmetry restoration crossover suggests that QCD is still in the confining regime with chirally symmetric quarks bound into the color-singlets by the confining electric field. This regime of QCD was called a stringy fluid. At a temperature T_d that is essentially above T_ch the chiral spin symmetry smoothly disappears suggesting that the confining electric field gets screened and one observes a very smooth crossover to the quark-gluon plasma. The three-regimes picture has been further substantiated by the analysis of the N_c scaling of the energy density, the pressure and the entropy density. In the hadron gas they scale as N_c^0, in the stringy fluid as N_c^1 and in the quark-gluon plasma as N_c^2. We have analyzed the fluctuations of conserved charges that scale as N_c^1 above T_ch thus indicating a transition from the hadron gas to the stringy fluid. When N_c gets sufficiently large the three-regimes picture transforms into the three-phases phase diagram. Finally we discuss a confining and chirally symmetric model in 3+1 dimensions. This model demonstrates the chiral symmetry restoration in the confining regime and a delocalization of the color-singlet quark-antiquark systems that become very large at T > T_ch. Consequently the stringy fluid matter is a very dense highly collective system of the overlapping very large color-singlet quark-antiquark "mesons" with a very small mean free path.
comment: 15 pages. Article commissioned by Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics. In v.2 the article has been essentially extended
♻ ☆ The Spectral Edge at Large Central Charge and Black Hole Statistics
Eric Perlmutter
We introduce a new approach to high-energy spectra in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, addressing the open challenge of incorporating spectral statistics into the modular bootstrap. Using the analytic theory of $L$-functions attached to two-dimensional CFTs, we leverage modular constraints among high-energy states to derive a sum rule relating the spectral edge to bulk spectral fluctuations. As an application, we establish a refined modular bootstrap bound: letting $Δ_1$ be the conformal dimension of the lightest excited Virasoro primary of a unitary CFT of central charge $c$, we show that $Δ_1 - {c-1\over 12} \leq o(c)$, with at most one exceptional value of the scalar gap at each sufficiently large $c$. The result applies to theories with logarithmic rigidity of spectral counting fluctuations, as in random matrix theory. We exhibit circumstances under which the bound is strengthened further.
comment: 33 pages. v2: improved proof, more explicit treatment and an added appendix; fixed typos; added refs
♻ ☆ Stationary solutions in the small-$c$ expansion of GR
Enes Bal, Ertuğrul Ekiz, Emre Onur Kahya, Utku Zorba
We study the small-$c$ expansion of general relativity in ADM variables up to next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO). We show that, in the stationary sector, this formulation renders the field equations more tractable for explicit solution building. The stationary equations acquire a structure, in which the leading lapse and spatial metric are determined by a closed subsystem, the NLO rotational field satisfies a linear equation on that background, and the NNLO fields satisfy a linear system sourced by the NLO data. The stationary sector exhibits both strong-gravity and weak-field branches, whose structure becomes richer at NNLO. In the strong-gravity branch, we first obtain exact vacuum solutions of NLO Carroll gravity, including the Lense--Thirring and rotating C-metric backgrounds. At NNLO, we then construct the corresponding Lense--Thirring-type and C-metric-type exact vacuum geometries. These solutions also arise from the small-$c$ expansion of the Kerr and rotating C-metric geometries around the strong-gravity background, up to $\mathcal{O}(J)$ at NLO and up to $\mathcal{O}(J^3)$ at NNLO. In the weak-field branch, we find exact Hartle--Thorne-type solutions with an independent quadrupole moment, together with exact spin-squared corrections and a mixed quadrupolar-rotating solution. We further extend the $\ell=0,2$ sector by including higher multipoles up to $\ell=4$, where $\ell$ denotes the multipole index. These results show that the full NLO/NNLO theory admits a richer stationary vacuum sector than the magnetic Carroll truncation. More broadly, the ADM formulation provides a practical framework for constructing and analyzing stationary backgrounds in the small-$c$ expansion of general relativity, and may also offer a useful framework for organizing rotational and higher-multipole deformations motivated by relativistic compact-object geometries.
comment: 38 pages; v2: 39 Pages, references and additional explanations added; v3: 40 pages, published version, one sentence added to the abstract, stationary ADM reduction and boundary conditions clarified, two references added
♻ ☆ A Note on a High-Energy Limit of Gravitational Perturbation Theory
Poul H. Damgaard, Ludovic Plante
The post-Minkowskian expansion of general relativity expands the metric in Newton's constant G around flat space-time, but much effort currently focuses on ways to extend its range of applicability by summing the perturbative series to all orders. A regime of particular interest is a specific high-energy limit where a formula derived recently provides the momentum kick of binary scattering problem to all orders, and even suggests an approach towards strong coupling. We show that this is an asymptotic expansion. Although the series diverges we give evidence that it is Borel summable, and the full function in integral form is finite. As a by-product we determine the transcendentality properties of the coefficients in the expanded expression.
comment: 7 pages, expanded description of asymptotic estimates and Borel summability. Version to appear in Physics Letters B
♻ ☆ Tidal Love numbers of wormholes as black-hole mimickers
Sergey N. Solodukhin, Vagif Tagiev
We study the dynamical scalar tidal Love numbers of wormholes that provide viable mimickers for black holes, focusing on thin-shell Schwarzschild and Damour-Solodukhin geometries. Using a matched near- and far-zone expansion, we determine their tidal response in the low-frequency regime. The presence of a long throat introduces an additional characteristic scale and naturally separates the modes into two classes. Super-throat modes probe the global wormhole geometry and are sensitive to both asymptotic regions, whereas sub-throat modes probe only one side of the wormhole and effectively perceive the throat as a black-hole horizon. We derive the scalar tidal Love numbers analytically for both classes of modes and show that their dissipative parts exhibit distinct low-frequency behavior, reflecting whether one or both potential barriers participate in the scattering process. We further find that, as the wormhole approaches the black-hole limit, the super-throat contribution becomes progressively negligible, while the sub-throat response smoothly reduces to that of a Schwarzschild black hole. These results demonstrate that the tidal response of wormholes depends crucially on whether the perturbation probes the global structure of the throat.
comment: 46 pages, 3 figures; V3: an Acknowlegments section and several references aded, accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. D
♻ ☆ Varying Newton constant, entropy and the black hole evaporation law
Julia Haba, Zbigniew Haba
We assume that the Newton potential of a spherically symmetric body of mass $M$ is $V=-G(M)Mr^{-1}$, where the Newton constant $G$ may depend on $M$. We insert this assumption in the Schwarzschild solution. We discuss varying $G$ in the black hole thermodynamics and black hole evaporation law. We extend the Bekenstein-Hawking formula $\hbar GS=\frac{1}{4}A$, where $S$ is the entropy and $ A$ the area, to a varying $G$. It is shown that if $G(M)$ is of the form of a power-law $G\simeq M^{-Γ}$ then $G(M)S\simeq A$ is still preserved but the evaporation law substantially depends on the function $G(M)$.
comment: to appear in Eur.Phys.J.Plus
♻ ☆ Black Hole Entropy from Entangled Quantum Reference Frames
Ludovic Varrin
In the extended phase space of Donnelly and Freidel, the edge modes of a Schwarzschild black hole are dynamical reference frames whose phase space is the cotangent bundle of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Gluing the two exterior regions at the bifurcation point leaves a single canonical pair. Within the extended phase space, this pair can be described either by Kuchař's mass and difference of asymptotic times or by the area and the relative rapidity of the two frames, which are two gauge choices of the same system. The latter is the pair of Carlip and Teitelboim, and the relative rapidity is the time shift of the crossed product construction. We quantize the frames in this gauge and construct the gravitational entangling product of the two exteriors. Requiring the frames to be causal restricts them to the semigroup $\mathrm{SL}^+(2,\mathbb{R})$, whose Plancherel measure yields the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy as the entanglement entropy between the two exteriors, together with a logarithmic correction, both independent of the ultraviolet cutoff.
comment: V2: Added references. 43 pages, 1 figure
♻ ☆ Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
Tao Li, Hai-Bing Fu, Lei-Hua Liu
We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) inflation. We construct the Hamiltonians from the quadratic actions and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing parameters. Although the tensor propagation speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss-Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We then calculate the Nielsen circuit complexity of the corresponding two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation between the squeezing amplitudes, while the squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Therefore, the circuit complexity is mainly controlled by the evolution of the squeezing amplitudes. For the benchmark parameters considered here, a positive coupling increases the preparation cost of the scalar Gaussian state but slightly decreases that of the tensor Gaussian state. The scalar sector is therefore more sensitive to the GB coupling, whereas the luminal tensor sector provides a cleaner probe of the pump-field mechanism. Their opposite responses provide a differential state-space diagnostic of the same EGB background.
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures
♻ ☆ Localisation of $\mathcal{N} = (2,2)$ theories on spindles of both twists
Imtak Jeon, Hyojoong Kim, Nakwoo Kim, Aaron Poole, Augniva Ray
We consider two-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(2,2)$ supersymmetric field theories living on a spindle $\mathbb{WCP}_{[n_1,n_2]}^1$. Starting from the spindle solutions of five-dimensional STU gauged supergravity, we construct theories on a spindle which preserve supersymmetry via either the twist or anti-twist mechanism and admit two Killing spinors of opposite R-charge. While the study of field theories on anti-twisted spindles has already been undertaken in some detail, the advantage of our approach allows for the derivation of analogous results in the twist case. We apply the technique of supersymmetric localisation to compute the exact partition function for a theory consisting of an abelian vector multiplet and a charged chiral multiplet in the presence of a Fayet-Iliopoulos term. We compare and contrast the results for the twisted and anti-twisted spindle and find a general formula which encompasses the partition function for both cases simultaneously.
comment: 38 pages + appendices, no figures; v2, minor typos corrected and reference added; v3, matches version published in JHEP
♻ ☆ Poisson bracket and $L_\infty$ algebras
Vinícius Bernardes, Theodore Erler, Atakan Hilmi Fırat, Igor Khavkine
We describe the Poisson bracket of a Lagrangian field theory expressed in the framework of $L_\infty$ algebras. If the symplectic structure on phase space is defined following recent work, we show that the Poisson bracket can be computed with the Peierls formula, confirming the well-known result of the covariant phase space formalism. Of particular interest is the Poisson bracket in nonlocal theories. In $p$-adic string theory we find that a straightforward construction of the Poisson bracket is obstructed by higher derivative instabilities. We also discuss the inverse relation between the Poisson bracket and symplectic structure in the language of homological algebra, extending some ideas in the mathematical physics literature.
comment: 27 pages, 3 figures; v2: minor improvements; v3: journal version
♻ ☆ Some universalities in the partition functions of low-dimensional gravity models
Mahdis Ghodrati
In this work, first, we discuss the connections between various low-dimensional quantum gravity models, including 3d Chern-Simons, 2d Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT), 2d background field (BF) theory, 2d Liouville, 2d Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW), and 1d Schwarzian, which are related through holography and dimension reduction, and discuss some universalities in their partition functions. Then, we specifically examine the JT partition function and the partition function of $\mathcal{N}=(2,2)$ on $S^2$ and $\text{AdS}_2$ and discuss their similarities and therefore examine our proposed universalities. We change the parameters in each model and based on the change in the structure of the partition functions, strengthen our conjectures. We also use eigenfunctions, spectra and the behaviors of Wheeler-DeWitt wavefunctions to generate more universalities between these low-dimensional quantum gravity models, specifically in their partition functions. Finally, we use entanglement entropy, complexity and RG flows, particularly in the context of wormholes, to find more universalities in quantum gravity models.
comment: 49 pages, 28 figures
♻ ☆ Holographic $s$- and $p$-wave superconductors from the $4D$ regularization of Einstein-Lovelock theory
Soodeh Zarepour, Ali Dehghani
We investigate holographically dual descriptions of $(2+1)$-dimensional s-wave and p-wave superconductors in the framework of regularized four-dimensional Einstein-Lovelock gravity theories, incorporating higher curvature corrections beyond the Gauss-Bonnet sector. We first implement the 4D regularization of Einstein-Lovelock gravity with finely tuned coupling constants to include corrections up to any $K$th order in curvature. The bulk geometry is constructed from exact black-brane solutions characterized by the fine-tuned Lovelock coupling $α$ and the highest power of curvature in the Lagrangian K. We then analyze the condensation of scalar and vector operators dual to minimally coupled matter fields, focusing on two bulk-field mass prescriptions, which significantly affect the superconducting phase. Our results demonstrate that higher curvature terms significantly modify the phase structure of both s-wave and p-wave systems and enhance the sensitivity of the condensates and critical temperatures to the gravitational couplings. In both cases, the critical temperature generally increases with the maximal curvature order K, leading to higher-$T_c$ phases compared to Einstein gravity, particularly for negative $α$. The coupling $α$ effectively governs the strength of higher curvature interactions in the bulk: positive $α$ suppresses condensation and lowers $T_c$, whereas negative $α$ enhances superconducting order and promotes higher-$T_c$ phases relative to Einstein gravity. We further study the optical conductivity and find that both the gap frequency and the ratio $ω_g/T_c$ exhibit a strong dependence on $α$ and $K$, deviating from the universal Einstein-gravity result. Higher curvature effects enhance the superconducting gap scale. Notably, the p-wave system shows a stronger sensitivity to the mass-fixing prescription compared to the s-wave case.
comment: 40 pages, 24 figures
♻ ☆ Framing Anomaly in Lattice Chern-Simons-Maxwell Theory
Ze-An Xu, Jing-Yuan Chen
Framing anomaly is a key property of $(2+1)d$ chiral topological orders, for it reveals that the chirality is an intrinsic bulk property of the system, rather than a property of the boundary between two systems. Understanding framing anomaly in lattice models is particularly interesting, as concrete, solvable lattice models of chiral topological orders are rare. In a previous work, we defined and solved the $U(1)$ Chern-Simons-Maxwell theory on spacetime lattice, showing its chiral edge mode and the associated gravitational anomaly on boundary. In this work, we show its framing anomaly in the absence of boundary, by computing the expectation of a lattice version of the modular $T$ operator in the ground subspace on a spatial torus, from which we extract that $\langle T \rangle$ has a universal phase of $-2π/12$ as expected: $-2π/8$ from the Gauss-Milgram sum of the topological spins of the ground states, and $2π/24$ from the framing anomaly; we can also extract the $2π/24$ framing anomaly phase alone from the full spectrum of $T$ in the ground subspace by computing $\langle T^m \rangle$. This pins down the last and most crucial property required for a valid lattice definition of $U(1)$ Chern-Simons theory.
comment: 7 pages of main text + 22 pages of supplemental material
♻ ☆ The Standard Model on a finite bosonic lattice with continuum Weyl fermions
Stephen D. H. Hsu
We investigate a formulation of the Standard Model with gauge and Higgs fields regulated on a finite bosonic lattice, while quarks and leptons remain continuum Weyl fermions. This retains the familiar continuum treatment of anomalies, spectral flow, and fermion zero modes. Standard Model anomaly cancellation permits a consistent, gauge-invariant phase for the massless chiral determinant. Yukawa interactions are incorporated with a gauge-covariant spectral cutoff acting on the interaction vertices, not on the fermion propagator. Under the stated analytic conditions, the cutoff can be removed by the local subtractions expected from one-loop power counting, yielding a finite, exactly gauge-invariant functional integral at fixed bosonic lattice spacing and spacetime volume, including topologically nontrivial backgrounds. At zero Yukawa coupling and on smooth weak-field backgrounds, we establish agreement between the appropriately chirality-matched overlap and continuum Weyl fermion determinants up to local counterterms. We also establish reflection positivity at zero Yukawa coupling and zero theta for a modified gauge-field reconstruction; its continuum equivalence with Craig's original reconstruction is not proved. The bosonic continuum limit remains open.
comment: 113 pages. v2 adds a weak-field equivalence result showing that Craig's overlap fermion weight agrees with the continuum Weyl determinant up to local counterterms. It also discusses Witten's recent eta-invariant formulation of chiral gauge theories and establishes its equivalence to the determinant-line phase prescription used here
♻ ☆ Asymmetric Dark Matter from Low-Scale Spontaneous Leptogenesis
Hiroki Takahashi, Juntaro Wada
We investigate a novel type of asymmetric dark matter (ADM) model in which the dark matter asymmetry and the baryon asymmetry in our universe (BAU) are produced simultaneously via low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis, where the mass scale of right-handed neutrino is much lower than the Davidson-Ibarra bound $M_1 \ll 10^{9}~\rm{GeV}$. In our scenario, both asymmetries are predominantly sourced by a dynamical $CP$ phase, namely the majoron. Its kinetic misalignment provides a sufficiently large, time-dependent effective $CP$ phase, allowing efficient asymmetry production even for low-scale right-handed neutrinos. In our framework, the sources of $CP$ violation responsible for the BAU and ADM are correlated with each other, leading to a predictive relation for the dark matter mass. In particular, when the dark matter asymmetry reaches its equilibrium value before freeze-out, the dark matter mass is typically predicted to lie in the range $\mathcal{O}(0.1)~\mathrm{GeV} \lesssim m_χ \lesssim \mathcal{O}(100)~\mathrm{GeV}$, which lies within the sensitivity of direct detection experiments. On the other hand, if the dark matter asymmetry does not reach its equilibrium value due to weak coupling, the allowed mass range extends over a broader interval, $\mathcal{O}(0.1)~\mathrm{GeV} \lesssim m_χ \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10)~\rm{TeV}$.
comment: 18 pages, 8 figures. Version published in Physical Review D
♻ ☆ Gauge-Invariant Fermion
Kang-Sin Choi
We show that in quantum electrodynamics the Green's functions of the Dirac-dressed fermion coincide, for any value of the gauge parameter in the $R_ξ$ gauge and to all orders in perturbation theory, with those of the undressed fermion in the Landau gauge. The dressed fermion couples only to the transverse photon, and the gauge parameter is confined to a decoupled sector. The dressed vertex then obeys a homogeneous Ward identity, and the dressed field is renormalized multiplicatively with no new counterterm. A partially dressed family realizes the Landau-Khalatnikov-Fradkin relation exactly, and dressings with other kernels reproduce other gauges. Every dressing yields the same pole mass and, with the differences carried by the vertex, the same mass function.
comment: 7 pages; v3: published version
♻ ☆ Analysis of Quartic Potential Problems Using Fredholm Integral Operators with Airy Functions
Ori J. Ganor
Fredholm integral operators that commute with the Hamiltonians of certain quantum mechanical systems with quartic potentials are introduced in closed analytical form. The operators are expressed in terms of the Airy function, and their eigenvalues fall off exponentially. Using these operators we obtain an exact dual description in terms of infinite one-dimensional chains. The systems discussed include the anharmonic quartic oscillator as well as multivariable potentials and higher dimensional systems. We compute a few moments of the Fredholm operators, using matrix models in the higher dimensional case, and we show how those can be used to approximate the energy spectrum and obtain estimates of the asymptotic behavior of the wavefunctions.
comment: 23 pages, 1 table. V6 has a reference added
♻ ☆ How does geometry shape quantum emission in rotating bumblebee gravity?
A. A. Araújo Filho
We compare propagation and static emission estimates in a rotating metric geometry and a stationary metric-affine bumblebee geometry. Their distinct constructions and spatial asymptotics are kept, and normalized Killing times define the physical frequencies and angular velocities. Direct invariant calculations identify the metric-affine outer root and open exterior axes as curvature singularities for generic rotation. The obstruction at bifurcation surface poles concerns the smoothness of the bumblebee field independently. Its mixed meridional component couples angular channels; finite transverse energy fixes the adopted axial condition and defines a self adjoint stationary operator on bounded exterior annuli. For the metric geometry, we construct normalized radiative scalar modes with specified Unruh data, evaluate the horizon frequency transformation, and include spontaneous superradiant emission through the radial scattering map. We prove positivity of the axisymmetric potential and compute numerical transmission factors and a partial scalar energy spectrum alongside an analytical lower bound. The static emission estimates use the stated Stefan-Boltzmann model.
comment: 48 pages and 12 figures -- version accepted for publication in EPJC
♻ ☆ Krylov complexity and spectral density of BMN matrix model
Dibakar Roychowdhury
We use Krylov complexity as a typical diagnostic of quantum many body dynamics in the context of BMN matrix model at large mass gap. We calculate several physical entities, for example, the moments and return amplitudes at large mass deformation. We calculate them for both spread complexity of states as well as Krylov growth of operators in the matrix model. We propose a general expression for the moments at any given order $n$. We also discuss orthogonal polynomials for spread as well as operator Krylov complexity. In the context of the Krylov operator growth we further compute the spectral function and the density of states. A careful analysis of the spectral function near the resonance reveals various IR divergences in addition to the physical collective modes. These collective modes appear to be exceptionally stable due to large mass gap. On the other hand, the UV of the theory appears to be extremely damped due to higher scattering rates. We carefully diagnose these IR divergences near resonance which reveals that these collective modes are in fact non-propagating and should be thought of as diffusion modes or relaxation modes with infinite relaxation time. We also calculate the Krylov variance and Krylov entropy for the matrix model and in particular at early time. The linear early time growth of the Krylov entropy confirms the onset of quantum chaos in the matrix model at large mass gap.
comment: v2, Accepted for publication in JHEP
♻ ☆ Perturbative Coulomb branches on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$: the global D-term potential
Arash Arabi Ardehali, Daniel J. Resnick
We develop a Wilsonian description of perturbative D-terms in 4d $\mathcal N=1$ gauge theories on $\mathbb R^3\times S^1$ with chiral Kaluza--Klein spectra. A closed-form, one-loop-exact coefficient of the auxiliary D fields, including 4d Fayet--Iliopoulos parameters and globally valid throughout the holonomy space, determines the leading holonomy potential away from massless thresholds. We establish uniform weak-coupling control there and match across thresholds by retaining the light fields. Gauge-anomaly cancellation renders the Coulomb-slice vacuum equations affine within each chamber bounded by the thresholds, enabling exact linear analysis of their zero sets and numerical reconstruction through DBSCAN clustering of approximate zeros, LPCA denoising, and RANSAC hyperplane detection. Complementing the rank-one applications of the accompanying Letter, we study flavor-twist dependence in the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ $\mathcal N=4$ theory, and illustrate the numerical reconstruction in higher-rank R-twisted Argyres--Douglas reductions of interest in the SCFT/VOA correspondence. We also relate the same D-term data to leading stationary-phase equations of supersymmetric partition functions and a decompactification limit of the torus twisted superpotential.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology 74
☆ Particle production from noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole
Alberto Maya, Marco Maceda
By considering a massless Klein-Gordon field and the moving mirror model, we calculate particle production for a noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole sourced by smeared distributions of mass and charge. We show that noncommutative truncated trajectories diminish the emission spectrum at large frequencies, due to noncommutative effects on the external surface gravity of the black hole, in sharp contrast with the spectrum of a classical Reissner-Nordström black hole.
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures
☆ The Double Copy of the Doubly Spinning Black Ring
Damien A. Easson
We establish an exact curved-background Weyl double copy for the doubly spinning Pomeransky--Sen'kov black ring. Its full Weyl tensor is a quadratic form in two source-free Maxwell fields: one generated by the stationary Killing vector, the other a flux-carrying magnetic field obtained by linearizing the dipole-ring gauge potential about its vacuum limit. The mixed Maxwell bilinear is essential: no spacetime-independent real or complex change of field basis removes it. We identify the inverse $S_{IJ}$ of the Weyl coefficient matrix as a matrix zeroth copy. The same matrix arises independently from a weighted limit of the inner products of two Killing vectors in a six-dimensional Ricci-flat parent and satisfies $\Box_g S_{IJ}=-\tfrac12 F_{I\,ab}F_J{}^{ab}$. The singly spinning limit recovers the diagonal two-field Weyl double copy of the Emparan--Reall ring.
comment: 4 pages, 13 Supplemental Material
☆ Edge dynamics of covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons
Erica Bertolini, Matteo Carrega, Nicola Maggiore, Daniel Sacco Shaikh, Maria Florencia Semino
We study the covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons in 2+1 dimensions in the presence of a planar boundary. The differential generator associated with the scalar gauge symmetry singles out a single scalar Ward combination of the functional field equations. Its zeroth and first normal moments give two integrated boundary identities. The zeroth moment yields a traceless rank-two current obeying a fractonic double-divergence conservation law and a higher-rank Kac-Moody algebra. The first moment makes the normal-tangential field $w_i=h_{2i}$ explicit and yields an ordinarily conserved vector current with a standard $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra. Functional differentiation also produces a mixed equal-time bulk-boundary commutator between $w_1$ and $h_{11}$: it is non-vanishing at finite normal distance and vanishes in the intrinsic boundary limit. The equal-time commutators of the boundary current with the spatial components of the gauge-invariant field strength vanish, so microcausality is satisfied; when the boundary parameters are such that the two boundary sectors decouple, its retarded response vanishes at all times. Locally, the boundary constraints are solved by $w_i=\partial_iχ$ and $h_{ij}=\partial_i\partial_jξ+η_{ij}φ$. When the boundary parameters are such that the two sectors decouple, the induced action is the direct sum of a chiral boson in the $w_i$ sector and a higher-rank sector in which $φ$ is auxiliary and $ψ=\partial_1ξ$ is the propagating field. The latter has a non-chiral Luttinger description on its positive-energy branch and admits a chiral reduction. The boundary conditions determine the velocity and positivity branch of the $w_i$ mode, while the compatibility analysis in the $h_{ij}$ sector selects the positive-energy branch. On the positive-energy branch the two chiral modes co-propagate with orientation opposite to the sign of $κ$.
comment: 37 pages, no figures
☆ Generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics from gravitational perturbations of near-extremal Kerr
Marcela Cárdenas, Benjamín Cuevas-Tapia, Jessica Trespalacios
We derive the generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics of near-extremal Kerr directly from four-dimensional gravitational perturbations of the near-horizon geometry. We construct two families of exact linear perturbations of the near-NHEK background: a non-normalizable mode that deforms the asymptotic boundary, and a normalizable mode supported near the horizon. Both perturbations are smooth solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations reduced to the Jackiw--Teitelboim equation for the dual scalar, without conical singularities. We study their asymptotic symmetries and show that they generate an algebra of time reparametrizations; requiring the gauge parameters to depend on the Schwarzian mode, the isometry condition selects the stationary KdV hierarchy. The same hierarchy is independently enforced by the vacuum Einstein equations on the perturbation coefficient. In the Euclidean regime, we evaluate the Hamiltonian action and show that each mode independently generates a tower of odd-power corrections to the near-extremal entropy.
comment: 29 pages
☆ Does DESI point towards transient cosmic acceleration?
Muhammad Ahmad, Saddam Hussain, Ayodeji Ibitoye, Yi'an Zhao, Ming Zhang, Lang Cui
We investigate an oscillatory equation of state for dark energy that oscillates around the mean value $-1$ and includes a source term proportional to the cube of the number of e-folds. Due to this source term, the oscillation amplitude shifts towards the $w_{\rm de}<-1$ regime at higher redshifts, whereas in the future, the source term drives the oscillation amplitude towards the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime. As the equation of state enters the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime in the future, the dark energy density dilutes, causing the Hubble parameter to decrease asymptotically towards zero, so that the present acceleration is transient: the Universe transitions to decelerated expansion and approaches a static state as $a\to\infty$, without ever contracting. We compare this equation of state with BellDE, CPL and flat $Λ$CDM. We confront the model with a combination of datasets, including Planck, DESI BAO and three different supernova compilations: Pantheon+, Union3 and DES-Dovekie. We compare the log-evidence of each model with that of $Λ$CDM. The dynamical dark energy models yield $H_0$ values in the range $66.0^{+0.80}_{-0.79}$--$67.84^{+0.69}_{-0.74}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, with matter density values in the range $Ω_{\rm m}=0.3067^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072}$--$0.3271^{+0.0083}_{-0.0080}$ across all the combinations. These values are consistent with those of the baseline model, apart from a mild upward shift in $Ω_{\rm m}$ for the Union3 combination. Among all the models, BellDE yields comparatively stronger Bayesian evidence than the other models, with weak evidence for the Pantheon+ compilation and moderate evidence for the Union3 and DES-Dovekie compilations. The sourced oscillatory model yields inconclusive evidence for Pantheon + and Union3, while weak evidence for DES-Dovekie relative to $Λ$CDM.

☆ Scalar Black-Holes in Gravity from Entropy
David S. Pereira, Udaykrishna Thattarampilly, Vishnu Kakkat
We investigate static, spherically symmetric black holes in Gravity from Entropy (GfE), focusing on the sector in which the bosonic form-space field is a pure scalar. Starting from the full auxiliary-field equations, we show that the Dirac--Kähler matter equation contains both a scalar equation and a two-form consistency condition. The latter is automatically satisfied by a radial scalar. We derive an exact integral identity, valid for a general backreacted static spherical geometry, and prove that a regular scalar approaching zero at infinity must vanish if the sampled scalar and radial auxiliary-field eigenvalues are positive and the effective mass squared $m^2+ξR$ is nonnegative. In particular, this excludes minimally coupled static scalar hair with $m^2\geq0$ on the regular identity-connected branch. We also present the perturbative GfE vacuum geometry and use its curvature to identify the region in which nonminimal coupling can evade the sign argument. A second, sharper estimate shows that making $m^2+ξR$ negative is not by itself sufficient to produce a regular static zero mode: a finite interval of nonminimal couplings still admits no branch bifurcating from the vacuum solution.
comment: 9 pages
☆ Quasinormal modes of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole: Linear stability and strong cosmic censorship conjecture
Subhodeep Sarkar, Suvikranth Gera, Avijit Chowdhury, Chiranjeeb Singha, Sreelakshmi Mundakkal Dasan, Sumanta Chakraborty
We present an alternative formulation of coupled gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black holes, yielding decoupled radial and angular equations with a well-defined $Λ\rightarrow 0$ limit. We compute the quasinormal mode spectra using spectral and direct integration methods, finding excellent agreement. All of these modes are consistent with the linear stability of the Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole. We investigate the photon sphere and near-extremal modes, revealing a non-trivial interplay between rotation and electric charge. We further explore the implications for the strong cosmic censorship conjecture and find that the photon sphere modes predominantly determine its validity within the parameter space considered. While increasing the rotation of the black hole generally favours the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, increasing the electric charge can promote its violation. We also find that the region of parameter space exhibiting a violation of the conjecture is comparatively smaller for gravitational perturbations than for electromagnetic perturbations. These results highlight the important role of rotation, electric charge, and the nature of perturbations in determining the validity of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in Kerr--Newman--de Sitter spacetimes.

☆ Mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of BDNK hydrodynamics: from heavy-ion collisions to astrophysics
Teerthal Patel, Henry V. Hirvonen, Fábio S. Bemfica, Marcelo M. Disconzi, Jorge Noronha, Jean-François Paquet
We present new developments in the mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of the causal and stable first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamic theory by Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha, and Kovtun (BDNK) in general spacetimes. We develop two independent flux-conservative algorithms for arbitrary 3+1-dimensional spacetime metrics. Both are hyperbolic, causal, and well-posed, pass convergence tests, and reproduce known results. The first uses a new first-order reduction with mathematically preserved constraints, whose numerical violations can be handled with cleaning fields (the resulting coupled system is proven hyperbolic and well-posed). The second uses a new mixed-order formulation, whose solutions are proven strictly equivalent to the original BDNK system, without cleaning fields. Our proofs rely on a new general theorem providing sufficient conditions for transforming a mixed-order system with arbitrary-order equations into a strictly hyperbolic system, strengthening a classical result by Choquet Bruhat for weak hyperbolicity. We introduce a new practical prescription for selecting admissible hydrodynamic frames for a broad class of equations of state, including nonconformal ones relevant to heavy-ion collisions and astrophysics. Our simulations capture viscous shock broadening and suppression of Kelvin--Helmholtz vortices, reproduce Bjorken and Gubser flows, and study departures from stationary ideal-fluid configurations in Michel accretion and rotating tori on fixed Schwarzschild and Kerr backgrounds. For heavy-ion collisions, we perform boost invariant simulations with a lattice-QCD-based equation of state and fluctuating TRENTo initial conditions, comparing BDNK with a minimal Israel--Stewart theory. The descriptions agree at small shear viscosity but can differ substantially at larger viscosities, particularly for early initialization with rapid longitudinal expansion.
