Proposals to detect gravitationally induced entanglement between massive particles offer a promising pathway toward probing the quantum nature of gravity. We perform a systematic geometric optimization and comparative analysis of Stern--Gerlach (SG) and Mach--Zehnder (MZ) matter-wave interferometers for this purpose, deriving exact analytical expressions for the gravitational phase of each configuration. Our first key result is that geometric optimization is indispensable. For commonly assumed experimental parameters, neglecting the optimization of geometric ratios can suppress the accumulated phase, and hence the detectability of entanglement, by up to several orders of magnitude. Second, we provide a complete comparative analysis of two SG orientations (linear and parallel) and three MZ orientations (translation-symmetric, mirror-symmetric, and parallel-arms). The parallel-arms SG and MZ configurations tend to yield the largest phase accumulations and are nearly equivalent in performance, whereas the translation-symmetric MZ setup exhibits destructive-interference nulls that act as blind operating points where detection becomes ineffective. These observations highlight the importance of geometry-aware design. A Monte Carlo error analysis of realistic fabrication tolerances indicates that the parallel-arms configurations are generally more robust, maintaining low relative phase uncertainty over broad parameter intervals. Furthermore, an evaluation of Bell violations assesses the feasibility and signal-to-noise ratio of each configuration. Our results identify geometric optimization, particularly through parallel-arms designs, as an important consideration for near-term experiments targeting gravitationally induced entanglement.

♻ ☆ Quantum Theory Over Dual-Complex Numbers

We take quantum theory and replace C by C[e] where e^2 = 0, i.e. we extend quantum theory to the ring of dual complex numbers. The aim is to develop a common language in which to treat continuous quantum physics and discrete quantum models in a unified manner, including their symmetries. Since quantum theory is linear, introducing e is enough to model infinitesimals. A first objection to this programme is that C[e] is not a field, since division by e is undefined, while quantum mechanics typically relies on division. A second objection concerns whether unitarity still makes sense given e^2 = 0. Hence, the core of this work is dedicated to proving that dual-complex quantum theory remains fully consistent. In particular, norm is preserved at all times, and renormalization never requires dividing by an infinitesimal. An equivalence with conventional quantum theory is demonstrated: the dual-complex extension of a parametrized quantum operation automatically provides a linear treatment of its first-order variations. As a first example application, we provide a unified description of both the Dirac equation in the continuum and the Dirac Quantum Walk in the discrete. We establish the discrete Lorentz covariance of the latter.

♻ ☆ Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics

Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\simλ/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.

The underlying coherent superposition of macroscopic quantum states is translated into the statistical properties of the integrated charge deposited in the detector circuit of a mode-matched heterodyne/homodyne detection scheme. At first, the dynamical evolution of a signal transmitted from an auxiliary cavity is employed to pinpoint a macroscopic switching event in a bistable main cavity subject to direct photodetection. Once the decision is made on the occurrence of a downward switch, the main cavity mode is let to freely decay to the vacuum, monitored to the production of an integrated charge. In the long-time limit, the charge distribution over an identical collection of pure states generated during the jumps converges to the Q function (heterodyne detection) or marginals of the Wigner function (homodyne detection) dictated by the phase of the local oscillator. When fluctuations over the ensemble step in, we connect the statistical properties of several switching events and the ensuing production of current records, to the cavity field correlations associated with the breakdown of photon blockade.

We likewise study the fidelity of SAGE two-qubit gates in the presence of charge and magnetic noise and again propose a simple refocusing strategy to mitigate the noise, while increased ramp times of the entangling pulse suppress leakage into noncomputational states.

☆ The 2d Ising Model on Hyperbolic Lattices and the Role of Boundary Conditions
Pallabi Dey, Debasish Banerjee, Arnab Kundu, Ritam Sinha
We investigate the role of boundary conditions in the critical behaviour of the ferromagnetic Ising model on regular hyperbolic tessellations. Using worm and Metropolis simulations, we compare open boundaries with wired boundaries implemented through a common auxiliary spin. For open boundaries, the susceptibility exhibits volume-based finite-size scaling with non-mean-field scaling exponents that are approximately stable across four tessellations, supporting the possibility of a common universality class. Comparisons with Binder crossings and susceptibility peaks reveal substantial finite-size effects. For wired boundaries, the central-to-auxiliary spin correlator exhibits radial scaling consistent with a mean-field magnetization exponent. The central-spin response to a uniform magnetic field provides a further consistency test of $δ=3$. Layer-resolved responses to a weak boundary field also reveal an enhancement of the induced magnetization towards the interior. Our results highlight the importance of boundary conditions and the distinction between interior and whole-system observables in characterizing critical phenomena on non-amenable lattices.

☆ Finite is not enough: Triviality bounds in nonlocal field theories
Fabian Wagner
An ultraviolet-finite theory need not be ultraviolet complete. This observation weakens the case for spacetime discreteness in quantum gravity if that case rests on removing ultraviolet divergences alone. We arrive at this observation by deriving the one-loop momentum-subtraction flow in four-dimensional $φ^4$ theories with ultraviolet-suppressing form factors. The suppression freezes the running above the nonlocality scale, but the theory can hit a Landau pole before suppression sets in. We obtain a bound on the infrared coupling by requiring perturbative control at all scales. This bound varies only at the percent level across the examples we consider. We expect similar bounds in models of discrete spacetime. Thus, requiring ultraviolet completeness improves the predictivity of nonlocal theories.

☆ Charged AdS$_{3}$ black branes as marginally deformed two-dimensional CFTs
Suting Zhao, Gabriel Arenas-Henriquez, Yizhou Lu, Hamed Adami, René Meyer
We study how boundary correlation functions encode the charge dependence of the renormalised Euclidean action of an AdS$_3$ black brane. In three-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell theory, the Maxwell field has logarithmic asymptotics and is locally dual to a massless pseudoscalar. In the canonical ensemble, the charge density fixes the slope of a spatially linear source for the dual marginal operator. At fixed temperature, the classical action is even in the charge density due to reflection symmetry $Φ\to-Φ$, and its charge expansion coefficients are governed by Catalan numbers. We compute the quadratic and quartic terms from connected correlation functions around the neutral brane. The scalar two-point function and the shift symmetry of its source determine the matter Weyl anomaly, which fixes the logarithmic temperature dependence of the quadratic term in the charge expansion. At quartic order, the connected four-point function comes from tree-level graviton exchange. Integrating it against the linear source, with an infrared cutoff on the overall scale of the integral, reproduces the quartic coefficient of the action per unit length. At each higher order, the corresponding Catalan coefficient predicts the integrated sum of all connected tree-level Witten diagrams.

☆ Running Couplings in CP Violating Abelian Theories
Joshua Newey, John Terning, Christopher B. Verhaaren
We calculate the one- and two-loop running couplings for a massless photon coupled to dyons, including CP violating couplings. The electric and magnetic source vertices in the most general theory form a real coupling matrix $C$, while a current-current interaction depends on $C^T C$ and the quantized determinant $\det C$. These determine, respectively, the continuously running Coulombic interactions and the fixed antisymmetric Dirac--Schwinger--Zwanziger charge quantization condition which also determines pairwise helicity. The running preserves $\det C$, showing that the electric and magnetic couplings run inversely while every pairwise helicity remains constant. We comment on how the running of the CP-odd coupling $θ$ relates to physical CP violation, which also depends on the spectrum, mass phases, and threshold corrections. We also show that an invertible field redefinition moves the CP-odd coupling between the current source terms and the photon kinetic terms; these are two descriptions of the same local interaction. Finally, we show that the result agrees with the Argyres--Douglas $β$ function ansatz.

☆ Constraint Variance Identity and the Matter-Geometry Fluctuation Relation
Yuki Yokokura
The quantum Hamiltonian constraint vanishes for physical states. For separable Hamiltonians in minisuperspace, its vanishing variance yields a fundamental identity. Under the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, we derive the Matter-Geometry Fluctuation Relation, dynamically linking spacetime clock fluctuations to matter fluctuations. This establishes a quantitative stability condition for the clock against total quantum noise. Finally, we obtain an uncertainty relation between matter energy and relational time. The stable existence of spacetime thus demands quantum fluctuations in matter.

☆ Chern-Simons Interfaces and Minimal Models from Quantum Groups
Suriyah Rajalingam Kannagi, Sergio Sanjurjo
Coupling two-dimensional fundamental Dirac fermions to $SU(N)_k$ Chern-Simons theory produces non-chiral interfaces that in the infrared flow to a compact boson and a $W_N$ minimal model. We propose a description of these interfaces as continuum limits of $q$-deformed fermion chains. The $q$-deformation is achieved by coupling a chain of one-dimensional fundamental complex fermions to $SU(N)_k$ Chern-Simons theory, keeping the underlying topological gauge field continuous. The operator algebra is controlled by quantum groups, which provide an algebraic perspective on the usual categorical formulation of anyon chains. As an application, we derive a Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraint involving baryon-number and lattice translation, obstructing a unique symmetric gapped ground state. At unit filling, we gap out the compact boson sector with a Mott term and obtain standard anyon chain Hamiltonians previously studied in the literature. This provides an anomaly argument for the existence of $N$ copies of minimal model sectors permuted by lattice translation in the infrared.

☆ Conformal Bootstrap Unblocked
Li-Yuan Chiang, David Poland
We develop a novel conformal bootstrap formulated directly in terms of conformal symmetry, reflection positivity, and crossing symmetry, without explicitly relying on the operator product expansion or conformal blocks. By constructing Gram matrices from states created by pairs of local operators and imposing spectral constraints through conformal generators, we obtain a hierarchy of semidefinite programs that directly constrain correlation functions. We demonstrate the method in one to three dimensions, obtaining correlator and spectral bounds that capture generalized free field behavior and reproduce the characteristic Ising kinks in two and three dimensions. We further show that joint positivity of states at different insertion configurations naturally constrains correlators away from self-dual kinematics.

☆ On Entanglement Dynamics in Holographic Theories
Hanzhi Jiang
Entanglement entropy (EE) is central to modern theoretical physics, yet its calculation in interacting theories with nontrivial time dependence remains challenging. In this thesis, we investigate the real-time dynamics of EE in strongly coupled quantum field theories (QFTs) using the Anti-de Sitter/Conformal Field Theory (AdS/CFT) correspondence. We first examine EE evolution in an exactly solvable two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT) with an inhomogeneous sine-square deformation (SSD). We argue that the unconventional time evolution driven by the SSD Hamiltonian can be viewed as a change in spacetime foliation, producing new horizons in the dual three-dimensional bulk. Holographic EE calculations agree with CFT results in all comparable cases. We then study entanglement dynamics in generic chaotic quantum many-body systems. In the limit of late time and large regions, these dynamics are believed to admit an effective entanglement membrane description. In 2d CFTs, a degenerate membrane tension reproduces several entropy dynamics results, unlike the non-degenerate tension in higher dimensions. Using holography, we show that capturing reflected entropy in 2d CFT requires an additional degree of freedom in the membrane description. We further show that a conventional non-degenerate tension emerges when the CFT undergoes a relevant deformation, holographically dual to a planar Banados-Teitelboim-Zanelli (BTZ) black hole with scalar hair and an interior Kasner universe. We then develop a membrane effective theory for reflected entropy dynamics in higher dimensions. Finally, we apply the membrane theories for reflected entropy to study the time evolution of multipartite entanglement signals. We found that scrambling dynamics generate multipartite entanglement with rich structures.

☆ To Infinity and Beyond: Maximizing Entanglement and Emergent Symmetries in $N$ Higgs Doublet Models
Spencer Chang, Gabriel Jacobo
In this paper, we explore the recent observation that maximizing flavor entanglement in Higgs boson scattering in a two Higgs doublet model leads to parameter space where the potential, if bounded from below, has an enhanced mirror symmetry $U(2)^2$. Looking at $N$ Higgs doublet models, we find a generalization of the mirror models, with $U(2)^N$ symmetry. Focusing on three Higgs doublet models, we determine that there is also a bounded potential solution that maximally entangles but has only the minimal $U(2)$ symmetry. This counterexample demonstrates that additional constraints must be imposed to maintain the connection between maximal entanglement and extended symmetries. As a potential constraint, for the three Higgs doublet model, we show that requiring maximal entanglement still occurs after gauging the symmetries eliminates the counterexample, thus restoring the connection.

☆ Asymptotic safety is not generic
Francesco Del Porro, Francesco Ferrarin, Alessia Platania
Asymptotically safe quantum gravity proposes a non-perturbative ultraviolet completion of gravity in which the high-energy behavior is controlled by an ultraviolet fixed point---the Reuter fixed point---for which there is robust evidence from a wide range of settings and truncations. The existence of asymptotic safety requires non-trivial zeros of beta functions, raising the question of how generic such fixed-point solutions are. In this work, we tackle this issue by investigating chiral perturbation theories. We focus on SU(2) and SU(3) chiral models, which share key features with gravity such as perturbative non-renormalizability or nonlinear interactions, but which are known to admit a different ultraviolet completion via new degrees of freedom. Using the functional renormalization group, we study these theories within a quartic-derivative truncation and find no evidence for an interacting fixed point. This result suggests that asymptotic safety is not generic, but rather a feature pertaining to certain special systems.

☆ Fermion$\text{-}$Monopole Scattering: A Unified Perspective
Hao Geng, Zekai Wang
We revisit the scattering of massless chiral fermions by a minimally charged BPS 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole. Existing proposals emphasize different aspects of this process and their connections are often unclear, giving rise to apparent conflicts concerning the outgoing states, energy conservation, and anomalous scattering amplitudes. We clarify the connection between different proposals within a common low-energy fermion-rotor description. Starting from the monopole background, we derive the rotor coupling and retain explicit fermion operators throughout the analysis. By adjoining a decoupled auxiliary scalar, we construct a dual theory that permits exact quantization. We show that the rotor vertex has a continuous spectral support down to zero energy and that its infrared exchange relations identify it as the twist dressing of the outgoing fermion. We also compute anomalous fermion correlators directly from fermion zero modes generated by winding configurations of the compact rotor. These results connect rotor dynamics, twisted outgoing states, and the zero-mode origin of anomalous correlators, resolving apparent conflicts and showing how the existing proposals fit into a mutually consistent picture within their common regime of applicability.

☆ Constraining the spectral gap of 2d CFTs just above c=1
Nathan Benjamin, Kevin Langhoff, Wei Li, Jesse Thaler
We numerically study the space of compact unitary two-dimensional conformal field theories (2d CFTs) with central charge $c>1$ using the modular bootstrap. We focus on bounding the spectral gap $Δ_{\rm gap}$ of such theories, namely the smallest scaling dimension among the non-vacuum primary operators. We use both a primal method that directly searches for consistent spectra and a dual method that yields rigorous exclusions. A key feature of our analysis is requiring the degeneracies of primary operators to be positive integers. At $c$ very near $1$, the integrality constraint greatly reduces the allowed spectral gap in both methods. For example, at $c-1 = 3\times 10^{-3}$ integrality strengthens the rigorous bound from $Δ_{\rm gap} \lesssim 0.5$ to $Δ_{\rm gap} < 0.041$. Our results suggest that the spectral gap might vanish as $c$ approaches $1$ from above.

☆ Matrix Theory from Holography II: Beyond Counting
Shota Komatsu, Eunwoo Lee, Chintan Patel
Extending our earlier realization of Matrix Theory for M-theory within AdS/CFT, we propose and test a new triality among a large-charge sector of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ ADHM theory, the BMN matrix model, and lightlike-compactified M-theory on the maximally supersymmetric pp-wave. In an appropriate triple-scaling limit, the superconformal index of ADHM theory becomes the grand-canonical index of the BMN model, with magnetic-flux sectors corresponding to fuzzy-sphere vacua. But the real interest of this new setup is that we can go beyond counting states. Using supersymmetric localization, we show that correlation functions in topological subsectors agree as well, including their nontrivial dependence on the BMN coupling. In each magnetic-flux sector, both the localization measure and the operator insertions can be matched precisely with those of the corresponding BMN vacuum. Our results also point to a deeper connection between monopole bubbling in ADHM theory and instantons in the BMN model. For minuscule monopole charges, ADHM correlators map directly to topological correlators in the trivial BMN vacuum. For non-minuscule charges, monopole bubbling produces additional screened sectors, whose relative weights reproduce the classical actions of BMN instantons. Mirror symmetry offers another perspective on this structure, mapping the monopole operators to Higgs-branch ``winding" operators in the mirror necklace theory. Finally, we discuss a type IIB counterpart, connecting a large-charge sector of four-dimensional $\mathbb Z_K$-orbifold quiver theories, the DLCQ of type IIB string theory on the pp-wave, and level-one mass-deformed ABJM theory on $\mathbb R_t\times T^2$. As a first test, we show that the superconformal index of the orbifold theory reproduces the vacuum degeneracy of the mass-deformed ABJM theory.

☆ Critical collapse remains discretely self-similar at large D
Christian Ecker, Florian Ecker, Daniel Grumiller
When matter collapses at the threshold of black hole formation spacetime typically has an emergent continuous or discrete symmetry, depending on the matter content. For the Einstein-Klein-Gordon model in any finite dimension D>3 the associated critical spacetime solutions exhibit discrete self-similarity, characterized by the echoing period Delta. Combining analytical and numerical results with dimensions up to D=200 we predict Delta remains finite at infinite dimension D, contrary to a recent conjecture. We find the fit Delta=1.6439+10.37/D-O(1/D^2) and provide an explicit large-D model.

☆ Multipartite Entanglement, TQFT Partition Functions and PL Bordism
Michele Del Zotto, Abhijit Gadde, Pavel Putrov
In a previous work we conjectured that the multi-invariants of the ground state of a gapped $(d-1)+1$-dimensional system, labeled by bipartite $(d+1)$-edge-colored graphs encoding closed oriented $d$-manifolds $M$, compute the partition functions $Z(M)$ of the low energy topological quantum field theory (TQFT), up to non-universal factors determined by the local structure of the triangulation. In this paper we determine which combinations of partition functions can be isolated from the non-universal factors. The answer is governed by oriented bordism. If $M$ is null-bordant, $Z(M)$ is obtained from an explicit, state-independent finite family of multi-invariants, up to a power of $Z(S^d)$ which is fixed to be $Z(S^d)^{χ(M)/2}$ for even $d$ and can be removed for odd $d$. Conversely, the obstruction is measured by a quotient of the group of "residues" of colored graphs which receives a surjective map from the oriented bordism group, with kernel precisely the torsion subgroup as far as smooth manifolds are concerned. In $d=4$ the obstruction is the signature: $Z(M)/Z(S^4)^{χ(M)/2}$ can be extracted if and only if $σ(M)=0$. This is due to the fact that the first Pontryagin class $p_1$ has a local expression and thus $e^{iθσ(M)}=e^{\frac{i}{3}θ\int_M p_1}$ cannot be separated from the non-universal factors. Torsion invariants, in contrast, are not obstructed: for the ground state of the $4+1$-dimensional invertible phase with partition function $(-1)^{\int w_2w_3}$ we compute the multi-invariants exactly, and two graphs with identical local data, encoding the Dold manifold and $\mathbb{CP}^2\times S^1$, give opposite signs.

☆ Conformal field theory from automorphic forms on a quantum group
Dalimil Mazac
We reformulate two-dimensional conformal field theory (2d CFT) in the language of noncommutative geometry. To this end, we introduce automorphic forms for the von Neumann algebraic quantum group $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. A quantum measure space is a von Neumann algebra equipped with a weight. We study such spaces carrying a weight-preserving action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. We argue that every unitary bosonic 2d CFT with central charge $c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2>1$ is equivalent to a quantum measure space with an action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})\times\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. In this dictionary, Virasoro primary operators are quantum automorphic forms and their scaling dimensions correspond to the spectrum of a quantum Laplace operator. The Virasoro crossing equations express associativity of multiplication on the quantum measure space. For compact theories, the algebra is a type III$_1$ factor. Liouville CFT is realized as $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$ acting on itself by left and right translations. Virasoro boundary conditions correspond to quantum measure spaces with an action of a single copy of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. When the boundary spectrum is discrete, these are noncommutative counterparts of compact hyperbolic surfaces. The formulation accommodates models both with and without extended chiral algebras. It bridges the Virasoro conformal bootstrap with categorical and von Neumann algebraic approaches to 2d CFT.
☆ Gravitational-Wave Constraints on $R^2$ Gravity
Pawan Kumar Gupta, Laura Sagunski
Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences provide a unique opportunity to test general relativity in the strong-field regime. Quadratic $f(R)=R+aR^2$ gravity is among the simplest higher-curvature extensions of general relativity and introduces a massive scalar degree of freedom whose finite interaction range can modify compact-binary dynamics and gravitational-wave emission. We map this theory onto the effective-field-theory waveform for generic massive scalar-tensor gravity, obtaining a theory-specific inspiral phase correction governed by the single coupling parameter $a$. Using Bayesian analyses of the binary-neutron-star events GW170817 and GW190425, we obtain a combined constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling of $a\lesssim6.2\times10^6\,\mathrm{m}^2$ at $90\%$ credibility, corresponding to a lower bound on the scalar mass of $m_s\gtrsim3.2\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. This constitutes the strongest astrophysical constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling, improving the previous best bound by approximately five orders of magnitude and demonstrating the sensitivity of binary-neutron-star inspirals to finite-range scalar interactions in the strong-field regime.

☆ Simulating a chiral gauge theory
Laurens Lootens, Hersh Singh
Chiral gauge theories underlie the Standard Model, yet none has been simulated nonperturbatively. Lattice constructions that evade the Nielsen-Ninomiya obstruction entail complex fermion measures or infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces. Here we provide a gauge-invariant Hamiltonian lattice regularization of 1+1-dimensional abelian chiral gauge theories built from clock-and-shift qudits with $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge fields, in which the global chiral symmetry and its 't Hooft anomaly survive exactly mod $N$. Anomaly cancellation on the lattice lets the Gauss laws be imposed and solved exactly, reducing the theory to an unconstrained qudit chain. Using infinite matrix product states, we simulate the canonical 1+1-dimensional chiral gauge theory, the 34-50 model, and find excellent agreement with analytic predictions, showing that a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space at $N=6$ reproduces the expected infrared physics of the continuum 34-50 model. This provides an efficient and practical solution to the problem of simulating general abelian chiral gauge theories in 1+1 dimensions, both on classical and quantum computers.

☆ Anomaly effective actions for 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories
Pantelis Panopoulos, Ioannis Papadimitriou
We present a comprehensive analysis of the Wess-Zumino anomaly effective action of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories in components. After reviewing the coset construction of the Wess-Zumino action in the presence of an unbroken subgroup, the gauging of the conformal algebra and the Wess-Zumino effective action for non-supersymmetric conformal field theories with a U(1) symmetry in two and four dimensions, we revisit the superconformal anomalies of $\mathcal{N}=1$ conformal supergravity. Solving the Wess-Zumino consistency conditions we determine both the bosonic and fermionic superconformal anomalies in a two-parameter family of schemes, to quadratic order in the gravitino. Turning on a chiral compensator multiplet and identifying a local super-Poincaré subalgebra of the conformal supergravity algebra without gauge-fixing the coset symmetries, we employ the coset construction and the superconformal anomalies in order to evaluate the Wess-Zumino action for generic $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories coupled to conformal supergravity. By construction, this action reproduces the Weyl, R-symmetry, and S-supersymmetry coset anomalies, but its transformation under the unbroken Poincaré supersymmetry differs from the corresponding anomaly of the conformal supergravity functional. We show that there exists a local functional of the coset-invariant old-minimal fields that, when added to the Wess-Zumino action, results in a generalized Wess-Zumino action that reproduces all anomalies of the conformal supergravity functional. The same local functional enables us to determine the super-Weyl anomalies and the Wess-Zumino action of old-minimal supergravity, providing a component version of the known superspace Wess-Zumino action.

Yang Li, Laurentiu Rodina, Zhi-Zhen Wang
We introduce a recursion based on hidden zeros that reconstructs complete tree level scattering amplitudes and one-loop integrands at generic kinematics. The recursion takes a universal exact-splitting form: both tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands are expressed as sums of products of complete tree functions, with the chosen zero conditions manifest in every term. We establish this structure for cubic scalar theory, the nonlinear sigma model, and inverse string Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) functions. We derive the tree splitting formula from the equations of motion, showing that hidden zeros arise when the product of two currents solves the equations of motion, while corrections away from the zero reconstruct the full amplitude. We further show that inverse KLT is the unique extension of $\mathrm{Tr}(φ^3)$ with higher-point non-derivative interactions that preserves hidden zeros.

We develop a microscopic prescription for determining 1-form symmetries directly from 5-brane webs. BPS Wilson lines are represented by configurations of D3-branes and $(p,q)$ strings, while their screening by local operators is realised through string junctions, Higgsing, and Hanany-Witten transitions. For O7$^-$-planes, the resolved 7-brane charges can be incorporated into the Smith normal form, whereas for O7$^+$-planes we propose an effective charge prescription and test it in both Lagrangian and non-Lagrangian examples. For webs with O5-planes, configurations of half-D3-branes reproduce the centre symmetries of Spin gauge theories and their breaking by matter. Crucially, we find that the 1-form symmetry of an O5-plane system is not determined by asymptotic data alone, but can depend on the local structure of the brane configuration near the orientifold.

Different situations are considered, ranging from a tunnel and mirror effect at low energy in front of a barrier, to higher energies, and also attraction rather than repulsion. The Kogut-Susskind (KS) formulation of gauge theories constructs quantum many-body Hamiltonians with gauge invariance under a compact Lie group exactly implemented on a spatial lattice. Here, we revisit this construction for a non-compact gauge group. Although motivated in part by theories like general relativity whose first-order formulation involves the non-compact Lorentz group as a local symmetry, we focus on simpler cases in one spatial dimension akin to the Schwinger model. In a bottom-up approach, we show how exact gauge invariance under the simplest non-compact Lie group ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ can be retained exactly on a 1D lattice, and highlight the differences that arise with respect to compact gauge groups, including a continuous spectrum of the Casimir operators of the gauge fields and the emergence of infinite-dimensional representations of the matter fields. For the pure gauge theory, we discuss how a consistent restriction to the positive semigroup ${\rm SL}^{+}(2,\mathbb{R})$ reproduces well-known results from the quantization of Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Motivated by the constraint structure of general dilaton gravity, we introduce static charges coupled to the non-compact gauge field, which can be realised by single-fermion degrees of freedom living in an additional, synthetic dimension. With static charges our lattice model remains exactly integrable, but when extending to dynamical fermionic matter, we arrive at an interacting 1D ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ KS gauge theory. We give an interpretation of this model as a chain of charges sequentially connected by strings whose tension pulls matter left or right depending on the sign of the relative continuous ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ fluxes. This picture becomes exact when the involved ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ charges are strongly self-interacting, where we solve the reduced two-body problem analytically.

We also provide an extensive and thorough review of quantum entropies, and we devote an entire chapter to the study of entanglement measures. Equipped with these essential tools, in Part II we study classical communication (with and without entanglement assistance), entanglement distillation, quantum communication, secret key distillation, and private communication. ♻ ☆ Einstein-Cartan pseudoscalaron inflation, reheating and nonthermal leptogenesis
Carlo Di Benedetto, Alessandro Di Marco, Emanuele Orazi, Gianfranco Pradisi
We study the postinflationary dynamics of an Einstein-Cartan-Holst gravity-motivated inflationary scenario, known as Einstein-Cartan pseudoscalaron inflation, coupled to a type-I seesaw extension of the Standard Model with three heavy right-handed Majorana neutrinos. In particular, we show that nonthermal leptogenesis emerges as a necessary and self-consistent mechanism for generating the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe, mainly because of the universal coupling of the inflaton to the additional heavy Majorana fermions. The resulting framework provides theoretical predictions that are fully compatible with the latest cosmological constraints from the Cosmic Microwave Background, Baryon Acoustic Oscillations, and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis, as well as with neutrino oscillation experiments, for a wide range of the fundamental Barbero-Immirzi model parameter $γ$, which controls the inflationary and postinflationary phases. In particular, for $γ\sim -1/100$ and a lightest Majorana-neutrino mass $\gtrsim 10^{13}$ GeV, we find a scalar spectral index $n_s \sim 0.970$, a tensor-to-scalar ratio $r \sim 0.004$, for a number of $e$-folds before the end of inflation $N_e \lesssim 60$, and a baryon-to-entropy ratio $n_B/s \sim 8.7 \times 10^{-11}$

♻ ☆ Galilean Kalb-Ramond Field
Aditya Mehra
We construct Galilean limits of the free Kalb--Ramond two-form gauge field and analyze their symmetries using two different procedures. An Inönü--Wigner contraction of the $D$-dimensional equations of motion results in two inequivalent electric and magnetic limits. In both cases the equations are invariant under the complete infinite-dimensional Galilean conformal algebra (GCA) only at $D=6$, the critical dimension of the relativistic theory. The second procedure is a null reduction of the $(D+1)$-dimensional theory which yields a local action for a four-field multiplet. In the zero-momentum sector, the resulting action is invariant under translations, rotations, Galilean boosts and an anisotropic dilatation with dynamical exponent $z$. However, in contrast to Galilean electrodynamics, it is not invariant under the special conformal generators of the GCA (and its higher modes). We attribute this to the vector residing at the bottom of the boost chain. If the parent theory is taken to be the six-dimensional conformal one, the resulting five-dimensional reduced action is invariant under the Schrödinger special conformal transformation with $z=2$ which is derived from the relativistic conformal group. In light-cone gauge, the non-zero null momentum sectors reduce to free Schrödinger fields. We obtain the gauge-fixed propagator, which is instantaneous, and compare the free-field correlators with the two-point functions allowed by the Ward identities of both.
♻ ☆ Bidirectional teleportation using scrambling dynamics: a practical protocol
Amit Vikram, Edwin Chaparro, Muhammad Miskeen Khan, Andrew Lucas, Chris Akers, Ana Maria Rey
We show that quantum information scrambling can enable a generic SWAP gate between collective degrees of freedom in systems without universal local control. Our protocol combines a Hayden-Preskill type recovery scheme, associated with the black hole information paradox, with quantum teleportation and runs them in parallel and in opposite directions, enabling bidirectional exchange of quantum states through global interactions alone. This approach cleanly distinguishes the roles of information spreading, entanglement, and chaos for enabling both coherent state transfer and recovery. We propose an experimental realization using the Dicke model, which can be realized in optical cavity and trapped-ion platforms, highlighting the utility of holography in designing practical quantum gates.

♻ ☆ Bootstrapping M-theory Orbifolds
Shai M. Chester, Silviu S. Pufu, Yifan Wang, Xi Yin
We analyze correlation functions of $SU(k) \times SU(2)_F$ flavor currents in a family of three-dimensional ${\cal N}=4$ superconformal field theories, combining analytic bootstrap methods with input from supersymmetric localization. Via holographic duality, we extract gluon and graviton scattering amplitudes of M-theory on ${\rm AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$ which contains a $\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{Z}_{k}$ orbifold singularity. From these results, we derive aspects of the effective description of M-theory on the orbifold singularity beyond its leading low energy limit. We also determine a threshold correction to the holographic correlator, which vanishes due to equal and opposite contributions from the two-loop gluon and the tree-level bulk graviton exchange.

♻ ☆ Rotation overcharges vectorized black holes
Shengjun Guo, Guangzai Ye, Peng Liu
A charged black hole has a ceiling: extremality bounds the charge that a given mass and spin can support. Vector hair has so far only lowered it. In the Einstein--Maxwell--Vector (EMV) model, where a massless vector field couples nonminimally to the electromagnetic invariant, the spherically symmetric vectorized Reissner--Nordström black holes are strictly undercharged: vector hair is paid for in charge. Whether this ceiling is a property of the vector field or merely of spherical symmetry has remained open, because spherical symmetry hides the hair's mass as well: its Komar mass vanishes identically and the exact identity $M_V=2Ω_HJ_V$ degenerates to $0=0$. Rotation lifts both degeneracies at once. We construct the rotating solutions of the model, the first in this setting, and find that the hair's mass is not a free parameter but a second-order invariant of the rotational response, fixed by $M_V=2Ω_HJ_V$. Above a coupling threshold the ceiling gives way: the domain of existence crosses the extremal Kerr--Newman bound, reaching $q=Q/M>1$ with $q^2+χ^2$ up to $1.84$, while at $α=5$ the maximum charge stays below it. The shadow is where the hair becomes visible. At $(q,χ)=(0.9947,0.10)$, near the extremal bound, the hair contributes an ellipticity of $8.30\%$, against $0.44\%$ from the charge and $0.06\%$ from rotation --- a factor of $19$ that charging a Kerr black hole cannot mimic; at the overcharged solution $(q,χ)=(1.2527,0.10)$ the total ellipticity reaches $25.6\%$. Whether the branch is ghost-free remains open, but the existing no-go criteria do not settle it: they assume a background and a dispersion relation that do not hold here.

♻ ☆ Cosmologically viable non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity: explicit models, $Λ$CDM limit and observational constraints
Emmanuel N. Saridakis
We investigate the cosmological implications of a phenomenologically relevant subclass of non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity (NPQTG), in which the background dynamics is encoded in a single function of the Hubble parameter. This framework provides a minimal and theoretically consistent extension of general relativity, incorporating higher-curvature effects while preserving second-order field equations and avoiding higher-derivative instabilities. We first establish the general conditions for cosmological viability and construct explicit realizations, including polynomial, quartic, power-law and non-polynomial models, demonstrating how different functional forms lead to distinct expansion histories. Focusing on the quartic and power-law cases, we investigate their late-time cosmological evolution, showing that they exhibit a matter-dominated epoch followed by a dark-energy-dominated epoch, and give rise to an effective dark-energy sector of geometric origin, with dynamical equation-of-state behavior that can lie in the quintessence or phantom regime. We then confront the models with observational data from Type Ia Supernovae, Cosmic Chronometers, and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations, using a Bayesian MCMC analysis. We find that both models are fully compatible with the considered data and reproduce the late-time expansion history with a quality of fit comparable to that of $Λ$CDM, although the current observations do not provide statistically significant evidence for a departure from the concordance scenario. Our results demonstrate that NPQTG offers a simple and efficient framework for describing late-time cosmic acceleration with dynamical dark energy, while maintaining theoretical consistency and observational viability.

♻ ☆ Factorization in deep inelastic scattering at Björken limit: Reduction to (1+1)D integrable models
H. Babujian, M. Karowski, A. Sedrakyan
We propose a Sine-Gordon description of the longitudinal sector probed in small-$x$ deep inelastic scattering on an effective string world sheet. Integrability gives nonperturbative access to the leading small-$x$ behavior through exact form factors. We test the proposal against combined HERA data with their published correlated uncertainties. In the window $Q^2>1\,\mathrm{GeV}^2$, $x\le0.01$, $y<0.3$, local powers describe the final reduced cross sections with $χ^2/\mathrm{dof}=71.811/77$ across 19 virtuality slices. Matching the measured exponent $γ(Q^2)$ to the exact Sine-Gordon power defines the scale-dependent effective coupling through $β^2(Q^2)/π=16/[3-γ(Q^2)]$. A bounded crossover with illustrative limit $C=0.431$ is compatible with the data; the compact HERA-I $F_2$ surface fit gives $123.608/106$. We also evaluate the fixed-coupling three-particle normalization, obtaining $g_3(\infty)=0.589320245$, verify numerical convergence independently, and derive its monotonicity and asymptotic approach. The proposed QCD correspondence is distinct from these exact-model and truncated-spectral results: identifying the collective world-sheet field, electromagnetic-current matching, and scale evolution remains an open problem.

♻ ☆ Comments on flavor symmetry breaking and three-dimensional superconformal index
Ilmar Gahramanov
We investigate the superconformal index of a three-dimensional $SU(2)$ ${\mathcal N}=2$ supersymmetric QCD with $N_f=4$ flavors. This theory confines with the breaking of a global symmetry. We obtain the index of this theory by integrating out a flavor from the theory with $N_f=6$ flavors. The superconformal index of the theory vanishes for generic values of the flavor fugacities. However, the specific choice of fugacities allows us to describe the flavor symmetry-breaking phenomenon.

♻ ☆ Quantum Advantage for Sensing Properties of Classical Fields
Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, Ishaan Kannan
Modern precision experiments often probe unknown classical fields with bosonic sensors in quantum-noise-limited regimes where vacuum fluctuations limit conventional readout. We introduce Quantum Signal Learning (QSL), a sensing framework that extends metrology to a broader property-learning setting, and propose a quantum-enhanced protocol that simultaneously estimates many properties of a classical signal with shot noise suppressed below the vacuum level. Our scheme requires only two-mode squeezing, passive optics, and static homodyne measurements, and enables post-hoc classical estimation of many properties from the same experimental dataset. We prove that our protocol enables a quantum speedup for common classical sensing tasks, including measuring electromagnetic correlations, real-time feedback control of interferometric cavities, and Fourier-domain matched filtering. To establish these separations, we introduce an optimal-transport conditioning method, and show both worst-case exponential separations from all entanglement-free strategies and practical speedups over homodyne and heterodyne baselines. We further show that when squeezing is treated as a resource, a protocol with squeezed light can sense a structured classical background exponentially faster than any coherent classical probe.

♻ ☆ Grey-body factors of black holes
Roman Konoplya, Alexander Zhidenko
Grey-body factors describe the frequency-dependent transmission of fields through the effective potential generated by a black hole or another compact object. They convert the idealized thermal spectrum of Hawking radiation into the spectrum measured by an observer, determine absorption and scattering cross sections, and provide real-frequency observables complementary to quasinormal modes. In this review, we present a unified account of grey-body factors in black-hole physics and related systems. We formulate the scattering problem for asymptotically flat, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter spacetimes, and discuss the connections between transmission coefficients, absorption cross sections, Hawking radiation, and ringdown. We also review methods for their computation and survey recent developments, including the correspondence between grey-body factors and quasinormal modes, their stability under deformations of the effective potential, wormhole transmission and superradiance, and their behavior in modified theories of gravity. Finally, we discuss the appearance of grey-body factors in gauge/gravity duality, where absorption probabilities in the bulk are related to correlation functions and transport coefficients in the boundary theory.
comment: Invited review for Reports on Progress in Physics
♻ ☆ Direction-of-arrival estimation of a gravitational wave by correlations between quadrupole moments of pulsar timing data
Taichi Ueyama, Hodaka Tamura, Hideki Asada
Can we estimate the direction of arrival (DOA) of a gravitational wave (GW) signal from pulsar timing array observations? The present paper addresses the inverse problem, for which we consider quadrupole moments of pulsar timing data due to GWs from a dominant isolated source such as a binary of supermassive black holes over an isotropic stochastic background. Correlations between the quadrupole moments are discussed as a possible alternative to the matched filtering technique, where the correlations between pulsar pairs over the full sky are taken into account. The correlations turn out to be in the form of a three-dimensional traceless matrix with rank 3 that can be closely related with a projection tensor for the GW. Thereby, we demonstrate that the rank-3 matrix allows to estimate the DOA of the GW without assuming a template bank nor a priori Gaussian noise. A mean over the celestial sphere is adopted instead of the pulsar averaging. A weighted average is used for a non-uniform distribution of pulsars on the sky, for which the Voronoi tessellation is employed to numerically calculate an area-weighted mean. In expectation of the forthcoming Square Kilometre Array, DOA estimation errors are also examined.

☆ A Transformer model for precessing binary black-hole merger waveforms calibrated to numerical relativity
Jameson Dong
We present a Transformer model for merger-centered gravitational waveforms from precessing binary black holes. Given the mass ratio and two three-dimensional spin vectors, the network predicts quintic B-spline coefficients for all 21 signed spin-weighted spherical-harmonic strain modes through $\ell=4$ on $[-1100,80]M$ ($M$ being the total binary mass), enforcing binary-exchange and equatorial-reflection equivariance and yielding $C^4$ waveforms in time with exact automatic differentiation. The model is pretrained on numerical-relativity (NR) waveforms from the SXS and RIT catalogues together with synthetic NRSur7dq4, SEOBNRv5PHM, and perturbative waveforms, and fine-tuned on SXS strain data. On 176 held-out SXS waveforms (165 physical systems), it achieves a mean balanced root-mean-square strain error of $0.023$ and a mean detector mismatch at $120\,M_\odot$ of $0.059\%$.
☆ Scalar perturbations in two-scalar-field warm inflation
Orlando Luongo, Tommaso Mengoni, Paulo M. Sá
We investigate scalar perturbations in a two-scalar-field cosmological model unifying warm inflation, dark matter, and dark energy. The inflaton is noncanonically coupled to a second scalar field that acts as dark energy at late times. Assuming negligible dissipation and perturbations of the dark-energy field, we derive the linear scalar perturbations in a gauge-ready form, including quantum and thermal noise in the inflaton sector and stochastic fluctuations of the energy transfer to radiation. We numerically solve the coupled perturbation system using a Fokker-Planck formalism and compute the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ for dissipation coefficients scaling as $T^p$ with $p=-1,\, 1$ and $3$. For $p=-1$, we find scenarios compatible with current CMB observations in both the weak and strong dissipative regimes, while the explored scenarios with $p=1$ and $3$ are outside the observationally supported regions. Compared with standard single-field warm inflation, the two-scalar-field model yields a systematically larger spectral index for a given tensor-to-scalar ratio.

☆ Noncommutative Kazakov-Solodukhin Gravastar
A. T. N. Silva, M. A. Anacleto, Ali Övgün, L. Casarini
We construct a thin-shell gravastar with a de Sitter interior and a phenomenological exterior combining a Lorentzian noncommutative-inspired mass distribution with the unexpanded Kazakov--Solodukhin deformation. Within an effective Einstein description, we derive the surface stresses, evaluate the shell energy conditions, and compute transparent-shell geodesics using a single exterior metric. The associated horizon-bearing family satisfies a radial-pressure thermodynamic identity with area entropy. For the gravastar, the first three penetrating visibility boundaries move inward with increasing KS scale, while the exterior photon orbit and critical impact parameter move outward. A finite-observer backlighting calculation reproduces the Schwarzschild--de Sitter benchmark and tracks the merger of visibility boundaries as the shell moves beyond the photon orbit. We also compute the redshift-weighted intensity of a face-on, optically thin emitting layer. Additional disk crossings after core transmission produce inner image structure whose brightness depends on the radial emission profile. At leading inverse-radius order, both deformation scales enter through one coefficient, producing an exact geometric parameter degeneracy. We show that the next inverse-radius term breaks this degeneracy: the critical impact parameter and logarithmic strong-deflection coefficient provide independent local information about the two scales. Full-metric calculations for equal-leading-coefficient parameter pairs resolve this splitting and quantify the accuracy of the higher-order expansion.
☆ Improving Gravitationally Induced Entanglement in Interferometric Configurations
Alireza Maleki
Proposals to detect gravitationally induced entanglement between massive particles offer a promising pathway toward probing the quantum nature of gravity. We perform a systematic geometric optimization and comparative analysis of Stern--Gerlach (SG) and Mach--Zehnder (MZ) matter-wave interferometers for this purpose, deriving exact analytical expressions for the gravitational phase of each configuration. Our first key result is that geometric optimization is indispensable. For commonly assumed experimental parameters, neglecting the optimization of geometric ratios can suppress the accumulated phase, and hence the detectability of entanglement, by up to several orders of magnitude. Second, we provide a complete comparative analysis of two SG orientations (linear and parallel) and three MZ orientations (translation-symmetric, mirror-symmetric, and parallel-arms). The parallel-arms SG and MZ configurations tend to yield the largest phase accumulations and are nearly equivalent in performance, whereas the translation-symmetric MZ setup exhibits destructive-interference nulls that act as blind operating points where detection becomes ineffective. These observations highlight the importance of geometry-aware design. A Monte Carlo error analysis of realistic fabrication tolerances indicates that the parallel-arms configurations are generally more robust, maintaining low relative phase uncertainty over broad parameter intervals. Furthermore, an evaluation of Bell violations assesses the feasibility and signal-to-noise ratio of each configuration. Our results identify geometric optimization, particularly through parallel-arms designs, as an important consideration for near-term experiments targeting gravitationally induced entanglement.
☆ Reanalysis of GW170817 and GW190425 under the Goldilocks Prior
Sanika Khadkikar, B. S. Sathyaprakash
Gravitational waves from binary neutron star mergers encode the properties of the densest matter in the universe, but recovering them accurately requires controlling biases introduced by the inference framework. The recently developed Goldilocks Prior incorporates correlations predicted by a large ensemble of candidate equations of state and broadens them according to the expected detector sensitivity. We apply this framework to GW170817 and GW190425 and find that the inferred component tidal deformabilities differ substantially from standard analyses. For GW170817, we infer both neutron stars to be more tidally deformable than previously reported, with the most probable value for the lighter star nearly doubling from $Λ_2\simeq215$ to $Λ_2\simeq443$ relative to the uniform-prior analysis. For GW190425, the Goldilocks Prior considerably reduces the range of allowed tidal deformabilities. We propagate the resulting event likelihoods to the dense matter equation of state using two complementary hierarchical methods, a strongly parametrized spectral representation and a broader semi-parametric Gaussian-process ensemble. For GW170817, both prior treatments yield consistent EoS constraints despite substantial differences in the inferred properties of the individual neutron stars. For GW190425, however, the EoS constraints differ beyond numerical scatter even after removing the source-level priors, showing that prior choice affects likelihood recovery for low-SNR events. The joint EoS constraints nevertheless remain largely unchanged because GW170817 dominates the inference.

☆ The Goldilocks Prior: Physically Consistent Inference of Neutron Star Properties from Gravitational Wave Observations
Sanika Khadkikar, B. S. Sathyaprakash
Gravitational wave observations of neutron star mergers provide a unique window into the interiors of neutron stars, probing dense matter from microscopic nuclear interactions to the macroscopic structure, including their maximum mass, beyond which the remnant collapses to a black hole. Accurate inference of these properties is crucial, as many astrophysical, nuclear, and multimessenger studies rely on gravitational wave constraints. Studies on estimating neutron-star properties from gravitational waves often employ priors that neglect correlations between parameters, or treat tidal degrees of freedom inconsistently, leading to biases in inferred neutron-star properties. We introduce a novel physically informed prior, Goldilocks Prior, that is informed by a broad, semi-parametric ensemble of equations of state, accounts for the joint correlations among the chirp mass, mass ratio, and both tidal deformability parameters, and is tailored to detector sensitivity. Using several mock binary neutron star merger simulations spanning symmetric and asymmetric masses, spinning and non-spinning systems, and a range of signal-to-noise ratios, we show that Goldilocks Prior consistently reduces biases in the inferred tidal posteriors relative to uniform and previously proposed EoS-informed priors. This framework provides a robust, systematic approach for neutron star parameter estimation, enabling more reliable inference for both current and future gravitational wave observations.

☆ Unruh-DeWitt detectors in a delocalized massive shell
Giovanna F. do Valle, Saadat Salman Shariff, Natália S. Möller, Nelson Yokomizo
We construct a model for the response of a detector to vacuum fluctuations inside a massive hollow shell in a superposition of positions. The delocalized source mass gives rise to a superposition of spacetime geometries and their associated vacuum fluctuations. To describe this system, we employ the formalism of quantum reference frames to transition to a frame in which the source mass occupies a definite position while the detector is in a superposition of positions. This allows the dynamics of the detector to be analyzed using standard tools of quantum field theory on a definite curved spacetime. We compute the detector response for a wide range of configurations of the shell and detector positions and investigate how information about the quantum state of the shell is encoded in the response function, identifying features of the superposition that are effectively captured by the detector. In particular, we show that, under appropriate postselection, the response function exhibits interference patterns, and identify regions of the parameter space of the model in which the shell-induced contributions to the interference terms are maximized.
☆ Coherent detector responses to quantum-controlled spherical-shell geometries
Shoshauna Gauvin, Robert B. Mann
A detector inside a static spherical shell samples globally matched field modes even though its local geometry is flat. We construct the response of a compactly switched Unruh-DeWitt detector on a quantum-controlled pair of transparent spherical-shell spacetimes with common Arnowitt-Deser-Misner mass. A stipulated common-incoming scattering identification places the branch excitations in one Hilbert space. Their positive Gram matrix determines joint, conditional, and dephased detector responses at a finite common readout, retaining the physical detector-clock phase in the uncompensated protocol. An additional coherent phase-gate protocol compensates free detector-clock propagation while preserving the shell interaction response. For concentric shells the centered response is exactly $s$ wave. A common incoming direction basis extends the construction to a lab-fixed detector and displaced shell centers, preserving common-translation covariance. The equal-radius benchmark exhibits conditional changes of order $25\%$ without dark-port amplification. Combining radius and position produces an assignment-odd response that reverses under reflection and vanishes at the relational midpoint. The relative normalized-state contrast reaches $34.15\%$ among the computed samples; the relative clock-resolved probe-influence contrast reaches $8.09\%$ for the declared readout, while larger values belong to its separate shared-phase envelope. These effects already occur in the dominant-energy-condition-compatible core. They are relational, model-dependent detector responses, not a background-independent witness of quantum geometry. First-order coefficients have finite pointlike limits; finite-coupling statements are made only at a fixed shared regulator.
☆ Finite is not enough: Triviality bounds in nonlocal field theories
Fabian Wagner
An ultraviolet-finite theory need not be ultraviolet complete. This observation weakens the case for spacetime discreteness in quantum gravity if that case rests on removing ultraviolet divergences alone. We arrive at this observation by deriving the one-loop momentum-subtraction flow in four-dimensional $φ^4$ theories with ultraviolet-suppressing form factors. The suppression freezes the running above the nonlocality scale, but the theory can hit a Landau pole before suppression sets in. We obtain a bound on the infrared coupling by requiring perturbative control at all scales. This bound varies only at the percent level across the examples we consider. We expect similar bounds in models of discrete spacetime. Thus, requiring ultraviolet completeness improves the predictivity of nonlocal theories.

☆ Analytic Marginalization Over Calibration Uncertainties in Gravitational Wave Inference and Application to Black Hole Ringdown
David Dzingeleski, Aaron Zimmerman
The uncertain calibration of gravitational wave detectors is one source of systematic error in gravitational wave inference. While generally small, this uncertainty can be accounted for by modeling and marginalizing over calibration corrections. In this work we extend the standard frequency-domain approach to calibration marginalization to the time domain using basis splines, in such a way that the marginalization is analytic. We apply this method to the time-domain analysis of black hole ringdown, in particular the two highest signal-to-noise events detected so far, GW250114 and GW250207. For GW250114 we continue to find strong evidence for two ringdown modes, after marginalizing over the small calibration uncertainty at the time of the event. For GW250207, the calibration of the LIGO-Hanford detector was uncertain, and calibration marginalization is required for a coherent analysis using both LIGO detectors. We find that when calibration effects are included the remnant mass and spins inferred during ringdown agree with inferences from the full signal. Despite the high signal-to-noise of GW250207, we find no evidence for the presence of a second mode in the ringdown, and as a result deviations from relativity during ringdown are not well constrained.

☆ Testing the Kerr hypothesis with orbital frequencies: lessons from spacelike singularities and black bounces
Hooman Neshat, Stefano Liberati
The inner horizon of stationary black holes is subject to classical and semiclassical instabilities, suggesting that the Kerr interior should be modified. Quantum backreaction may drive the curvature to the Planck scale, producing a spacelike singularity, or halt its growth at lower curvatures, leading to a regular black bounce. We investigate the phenomenology of these two possibilities using, respectively, a Gürses--Gürsey geometry with a spacelike singularity and the rotating Simpson--Visser black bounce. Both geometries reproduce the light ring and ISCO frequencies of a Kerr black hole with the same ADM mass and angular momentum, by calibration in the first case and identically in the second. We find that the null and timelike convergence conditions are violated outside the horizon, up to a finite radius beyond the light ring in the Gürses--Gürsey geometry and everywhere in the rotating Simpson--Visser spacetime. Moreover, their fundamental scalar quasinormal modes deviate from those of Kerr, most markedly in the damping, which is enhanced in the Gürses--Gürsey geometry and reduced in the rotating Simpson--Visser one. Thus, agreement with Kerr in a limited set of observables is not sufficient to establish the Kerr nature of a compact object, motivating complementary observational tests.
☆ Charged AdS$_{3}$ black branes as marginally deformed two-dimensional CFTs
Suting Zhao, Gabriel Arenas-Henriquez, Yizhou Lu, Hamed Adami, René Meyer
We study how boundary correlation functions encode the charge dependence of the renormalised Euclidean action of an AdS$_3$ black brane. In three-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell theory, the Maxwell field has logarithmic asymptotics and is locally dual to a massless pseudoscalar. In the canonical ensemble, the charge density fixes the slope of a spatially linear source for the dual marginal operator. At fixed temperature, the classical action is even in the charge density due to reflection symmetry $Φ\to-Φ$, and its charge expansion coefficients are governed by Catalan numbers. We compute the quadratic and quartic terms from connected correlation functions around the neutral brane. The scalar two-point function and the shift symmetry of its source determine the matter Weyl anomaly, which fixes the logarithmic temperature dependence of the quadratic term in the charge expansion. At quartic order, the connected four-point function comes from tree-level graviton exchange. Integrating it against the linear source, with an infrared cutoff on the overall scale of the integral, reproduces the quartic coefficient of the action per unit length. At each higher order, the corresponding Catalan coefficient predicts the integrated sum of all connected tree-level Witten diagrams.

☆ Constraint Variance Identity and the Matter-Geometry Fluctuation Relation
Yuki Yokokura
The quantum Hamiltonian constraint vanishes for physical states. For separable Hamiltonians in minisuperspace, its vanishing variance yields a fundamental identity. Under the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, we derive the Matter-Geometry Fluctuation Relation, dynamically linking spacetime clock fluctuations to matter fluctuations. This establishes a quantitative stability condition for the clock against total quantum noise. Finally, we obtain an uncertainty relation between matter energy and relational time. The stable existence of spacetime thus demands quantum fluctuations in matter.

☆ On Entanglement Dynamics in Holographic Theories
Hanzhi Jiang
Entanglement entropy (EE) is central to modern theoretical physics, yet its calculation in interacting theories with nontrivial time dependence remains challenging. In this thesis, we investigate the real-time dynamics of EE in strongly coupled quantum field theories (QFTs) using the Anti-de Sitter/Conformal Field Theory (AdS/CFT) correspondence. We first examine EE evolution in an exactly solvable two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT) with an inhomogeneous sine-square deformation (SSD). We argue that the unconventional time evolution driven by the SSD Hamiltonian can be viewed as a change in spacetime foliation, producing new horizons in the dual three-dimensional bulk. Holographic EE calculations agree with CFT results in all comparable cases. We then study entanglement dynamics in generic chaotic quantum many-body systems. In the limit of late time and large regions, these dynamics are believed to admit an effective entanglement membrane description. In 2d CFTs, a degenerate membrane tension reproduces several entropy dynamics results, unlike the non-degenerate tension in higher dimensions. Using holography, we show that capturing reflected entropy in 2d CFT requires an additional degree of freedom in the membrane description. We further show that a conventional non-degenerate tension emerges when the CFT undergoes a relevant deformation, holographically dual to a planar Banados-Teitelboim-Zanelli (BTZ) black hole with scalar hair and an interior Kasner universe. We then develop a membrane effective theory for reflected entropy dynamics in higher dimensions. Finally, we apply the membrane theories for reflected entropy to study the time evolution of multipartite entanglement signals. We found that scrambling dynamics generate multipartite entanglement with rich structures.

☆ Asymptotic safety is not generic
Francesco Del Porro, Francesco Ferrarin, Alessia Platania
Asymptotically safe quantum gravity proposes a non-perturbative ultraviolet completion of gravity in which the high-energy behavior is controlled by an ultraviolet fixed point---the Reuter fixed point---for which there is robust evidence from a wide range of settings and truncations. The existence of asymptotic safety requires non-trivial zeros of beta functions, raising the question of how generic such fixed-point solutions are. In this work, we tackle this issue by investigating chiral perturbation theories. We focus on SU(2) and SU(3) chiral models, which share key features with gravity such as perturbative non-renormalizability or nonlinear interactions, but which are known to admit a different ultraviolet completion via new degrees of freedom. Using the functional renormalization group, we study these theories within a quartic-derivative truncation and find no evidence for an interacting fixed point. This result suggests that asymptotic safety is not generic, but rather a feature pertaining to certain special systems.

☆ Critical collapse remains discretely self-similar at large D
Christian Ecker, Florian Ecker, Daniel Grumiller
When matter collapses at the threshold of black hole formation spacetime typically has an emergent continuous or discrete symmetry, depending on the matter content. ♻ ☆ Revisiting the Lyth bound constraints on inflation from ACT DR6 results
Rui Yang, Jun Tao, Peng Wang, Mian Zhu
The Lyth bound asserts that the field excursion of inflaton must be sub-Planckian, thereby imposing an upper bound on the amplitude of the tensor power spectrum in inflationary scenario. This bound is conventionally derived assuming a scale-invariant curvature power spectrum, i.e., $n_s = 1$. However, astrophysical observations confirm a red-tilted spectrum with $n_s < 1$. In light of recent results from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6, we revisit these constraints using the newly implied scalar spectral index of $n_s \simeq 0.9743$. Incorporating the ACT data yields a different upper bound on the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, which can potentially exclude inflationary scenarios previously robust under the original Lyth bound with $n_s = 1$. Our result highlights the urgent need to combine theoretical Lyth bound considerations with the most up-to-date astrophysical data.

♻ ☆ Accretion-powered flares from black hole-disk collisions in galactic nuclei

Black hole impacts on accretion discs in galactic nuclei can power luminous transients, but predicting their observable signatures is challenging because the post-collision flow is highly time-dependent and inhomogeneous. We present a radiative post-processing framework for relativistic hydrodynamics simulations of black hole-disc collisions. Using physically motivated prescriptions for shock heating, optical depth via an eikonal solver, and photon escape fractions that account for photon trapping and diffusion, we predict light curves and spectral energy distributions over a range of disc densities and collision velocities. Our results indicate that the emission is dominated by the long-lived accretion flow onto the secondary black hole, whose mass supply is highly super-Eddington, rather than by cooling of the unbound ejecta. In the parameter range explored, the luminosity is typically of the order of the Eddington luminosity of the secondary and can reach several times this value, and the emission is generically dominated by soft X-rays. We find that lower velocity collisions produce brighter flares, while the disc surface density mainly controls spectral evolution: low-density discs typically produce $\sim$keV-peaked flares with weak spectral evolution, whereas high-density discs show softer early emission and late-time hardening. A depletion-time estimate calibrated to our results suggests characteristic durations of hours to days for intermediate-mass secondaries, and yields $t_{\rm flare} \propto P_{\rm QPE}$. We discuss implications for QPE-like transients and for the SMBH-binary candidate OJ 287. Our framework does not include radiative feedback on the gas, therefore the luminosities should be interpreted only as baseline estimates of the available power for radiation.

Working within the metric-affine formulation, we adopt the regular, constant-$Q$ branch ($Q = Q_*$) of $f(Q)$ gravity, which preserves regularity at the stellar centre while maintaining explicit dependence on the non-linear functional form through $f(Q_*)$ and its derivatives. We propose three novel non-linear $f(Q)$ extensions: (i) a Born-Infeld-inspired model, (ii) a Hu--Sawicki analogue, and (iii) a Tsujikawa-inspired model. Incorporating state-of-the-art realistic unified equations of state, namely GPPVA(DD2) and SLy4, we numerically solve the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations and evaluate stellar stability via the Harrison-Zel'dovich-Novikov criterion. The Born-Infeld and Hu-Sawicki analogues smoothly recover the general relativistic limit as their control parameters increase, predicting stellar radii for low-mass objects ($M < 2.0\,M_\odot$) that match observational constraints from X-ray binaries and GW170817; however, their maximum masses remain capped below $2.43\,M_\odot$ (DD2) and $2.06\,M_\odot$ (SLy4). Conversely, the Tsujikawa-inspired model significantly stiffens the effective gravitational coupling, accommodating massive compact objects up to $\sim 3.36\,M_\odot$ and offering a viable physical origin for the $2.59_{-0.09}^{+0.08}\,M_\odot$ secondary object in GW190814, albeit at the expense of overpredicting radii for typical low-mass neutron stars. These contrasting behaviours demonstrate a key phenomenological complementarity between maximum mass and radius bounds within the constant-$Q$ framework, highlighting the utility of multimessenger observations in constraining non-linear non-metricity gravity.

♻ ☆ Rotation overcharges vectorized black holes
Shengjun Guo, Guangzai Ye, Peng Liu
A charged black hole has a ceiling: extremality bounds the charge that a given mass and spin can support. Vector hair has so far only lowered it. In the Einstein--Maxwell--Vector (EMV) model, where a massless vector field couples nonminimally to the electromagnetic invariant, the spherically symmetric vectorized Reissner--Nordström black holes are strictly undercharged: vector hair is paid for in charge. Whether this ceiling is a property of the vector field or merely of spherical symmetry has remained open, because spherical symmetry hides the hair's mass as well: its Komar mass vanishes identically and the exact identity $M_V=2Ω_HJ_V$ degenerates to $0=0$. Rotation lifts both degeneracies at once. We construct the rotating solutions of the model, the first in this setting, and find that the hair's mass is not a free parameter but a second-order invariant of the rotational response, fixed by $M_V=2Ω_HJ_V$. Above a coupling threshold the ceiling gives way: the domain of existence crosses the extremal Kerr--Newman bound, reaching $q=Q/M>1$ with $q^2+χ^2$ up to $1.84$, while at $α=5$ the maximum charge stays below it. The shadow is where the hair becomes visible. At $(q,χ)=(0.9947,0.10)$, near the extremal bound, the hair contributes an ellipticity of $8.30\%$, against $0.44\%$ from the charge and $0.06\%$ from rotation --- a factor of $19$ that charging a Kerr black hole cannot mimic; at the overcharged solution $(q,χ)=(1.2527,0.10)$ the total ellipticity reaches $25.6\%$. Whether the branch is ghost-free remains open, but the existing no-go criteria do not settle it: they assume a background and a dispersion relation that do not hold here.

♻ ☆ Cosmologically viable non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity: explicit models, $Λ$CDM limit and observational constraints

We investigate the cosmological implications of a phenomenologically relevant subclass of non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity (NPQTG), in which the background dynamics is encoded in a single function of the Hubble parameter. This framework provides a minimal and theoretically consistent extension of general relativity, incorporating higher-curvature effects while preserving second-order field equations and avoiding higher-derivative instabilities. We first establish the general conditions for cosmological viability and construct explicit realizations, including polynomial, quartic, power-law and non-polynomial models, demonstrating how different functional forms lead to distinct expansion histories. Focusing on the quartic and power-law cases, we investigate their late-time cosmological evolution, showing that they exhibit a matter-dominated epoch followed by a dark-energy-dominated epoch, and give rise to an effective dark-energy sector of geometric origin, with dynamical equation-of-state behavior that can lie in the quintessence or phantom regime. We then confront the models with observational data from Type Ia Supernovae, Cosmic Chronometers, and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations, using a Bayesian MCMC analysis. We find that both models are fully compatible with the considered data and reproduce the late-time expansion history with a quality of fit comparable to that of $Λ$CDM, although the current observations do not provide statistically significant evidence for a departure from the concordance scenario. Our results demonstrate that NPQTG offers a simple and efficient framework for describing late-time cosmic acceleration with dynamical dark energy, while maintaining theoretical consistency and observational viability.

At $a=1$, the GMGHS defect curve approaches a nonzero lower inverse temperature endpoint and contains a single unstable branch. In particular, the magnetic GMGHS black hole provides an explicit realization of the previously proposed $\overline W^{1-}$ thermodynamic topological subclass within an asymptotically flat Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton solution. This result demonstrates that the global topological number $W$ alone does not completely characterize black hole thermodynamic topology. The asymptotic behavior of the inverse Hawking temperature near the boundaries of the physical horizon domain provides an additional criterion for distinguishing thermodynamic topological subclasses with the same $W$.

A well motivated potential function and the linear form of the functional $f(R,L_m,T)$ have been incorporated into the Friedmann equation, and the autonomous dynamical system has been framed by introducing dimensionless variables. The stability behavior of the critical points is obtained and analyzed based on their corresponding eigenvalues. Moreover, cosmological parameters such as the deceleration parameter and the dynamical parameters such as equation of state and density parameters are obtained using the dimensionless variables. It has been observed that the system provides critical points that describe different evolutionary phases of the Universe.
